Over the past year and a half, China has shown the world the power of its economic arsenal—starting with the United States. In April 2025, Beijing retaliated forcefully against U.S. tariffs, imposing matching across-the-board levies and export controls on rare-earth elements. This counterpunch rattled bond markets and disrupted auto supply chains, forcing Washington to seek a truce that persists to this day.
Next, China targeted Japan. After Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described a potential Chinese naval blockade of Taiwan as a “survival-threatening situation” that could justify deploying Japan’s Self-Defense Forces, in November 2025, Beijing imposed suffocating bans on rare-earth exports to the country. Reluctant to reinflame tensions with Beijing, Washington offered nothing more than token support. Tokyo has held firm, refusing to walk back Takaichi’s statement; the restrictions remain in force, and Japan’s mineral stockpiles are dwindling.
Then Europe came under fire. Fed up with a trade deficit with China that had reached $1.1 billion per day, the European Union began exploring new tariffs to counter Chinese overcapacity in May. As China threatened “resolute countermeasures,” French President Emmanuel Macron urged U.S. President Donald Trump at the G-7 summit in June to join forces in addressing global imbalances. But the United States elected to sit on the sidelines again, and Europe blinked, opting for talks with Beijing, with an October deadline set by Europe to take concrete steps toward reducing China’s trade surplus. The EU has since been in tense negotiations with Beijing over reducing exports of hybrid vehicles, chemicals, and machinery, taking on the threat of Chinese retaliation alone.
China, in other words, is exploiting the disunity between the United States and its partners. In a divide-and-conquer strategy that mirrors the Trump administration’s own globe-spanning tariff campaign, Beijing has broken the Western alliance into more manageable pieces, allowing it to fight actors one on one. Its market heft and control over critical minerals have been decisive, and as its fear of retaliation has diminished, it has rolled out more aggressive export restrictions and sanctions. In 2023 and 2024, Beijing added only five Western companies to its Unreliable Entity List, exposing them to financial and legal penalties; in 2025 alone, it added 76.
There is still hope for the United States and its allies—if they can relearn to act in concert. These countries should build a formal economic security alliance that establishes collective defense against economic coercion. The foundation of this alliance would be a pledge modeled on NATO’s Article 5, which considers an attack on one as an attack on all, in this case promising a joint response to economic coercion against any member of the alliance. Over time, this alliance could grow to address other economic challenges shared by members, just as NATO began as a security guarantee before evolving into a more integrated and expansive military alliance. It could adopt joint tariffs against Chinese overcapacity and currency manipulation, coordinate investment restrictions and export controls on advanced technology, and cooperate on critical minerals and AI development.
Amid transatlantic squabbles and European calls for “strategic autonomy,” a Western economic security alliance may seem more out of reach today than ever before. But enduring interests can outweigh temporary political friction. With the right policy shifts and trust-building measures—starting with the removal of Trump’s tariffs on allies and legislation that limits the U.S. president’s ability to reimpose them in the future—Washington can forge such a partnership and use it to check Chinese coercion.
The United States, Europe, and Japan are all confronting a major shared challenge: Beijing is intent on making the rest of the world more dependent on China and China less dependent on the rest of the world. Beijing subsidizes domestic production far beyond local demand, undervalues its currency by 20 to 30 percent, and enacts coercive economic measures—such as export controls and sanctions—to gain leverage over Western governments and companies and undermine policies it deems against its interest. The country’s resulting industrial overcapacity and surging exports, epitomized by a record $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, threatens U.S., European, and Japanese industrial competitiveness and jobs. Beijing’s record of weaponizing its strengths also means that Chinese advancements in frontier technologies, such as artificial intelligence and connected vehicles, which continuously share data with external devices, pose security threats to Washington and all its partners.
Individually, the United States and its allies may struggle to match Beijing’s economic leverage, particularly its chokehold on rare-earth elements. But collectively, they are far stronger. The United States, Europe, and Japan alone produce around three times the amount of economic output that China does. They are home to the vast majority of the world’s most sophisticated companies. They also control critical inputs that China depends on, including lithography machines, specialized machinery for industrial production, chemicals, and aircraft engines. Despite efforts to reduce its dependence on the dollar, Beijing remains exposed to U.S. financial sanctions; only about 30 percent of China’s trade is settled in renminbi, and most of the rest is settled in dollars. The scholars Stephen Brooks and Ben Vagle have estimated that if the United States and its allies were to fully decouple from China, the harm to China’s GDP in the short run would be five to 11 times larger than that to U.S. GDP.
China is also more vulnerable than it appears. Despite an official GDP growth rate of five percent last year, the economic research firm Rhodium Group estimated that the country’s actual growth rate was 2.5 to 3.0 percent. China is undergoing a prolonged real estate crisis, state-driven overinvestment, and anemic domestic demand. With Beijing unwilling to address weak consumption, exports now fuel more than half of the country’s growth, according to Rhodium’s numbers, making access to Western markets China’s economic Achilles’ heel.
European businesses want to maintain ties with the United States.
If history is any guide, these Western states should be able to coordinate to use their collective power. During the Cold War, they came together to form the Coordinating Committee for Multilateral Export Controls to restrict sales of military and dual-use technology to the Soviet Union. After the 1973 Arab oil embargo, Canada, Japan, the United States, and a large group of European countries established the International Energy Agency, which required members to share reserves with any member affected by a supply cut—effectively a mutual defense pact for energy. And during the 2008 financial crisis, the U.S. Federal Reserve and other allied central banks coordinated rate cuts and established emergency swap lines to avert another Great Depression.
Yet in recent years, collective economic initiatives among Western allies have been underwhelming. In 2021, the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council was created to coordinate industrial policy and export controls toward China, but it largely devolved into a talk shop. In 2023, the EU established its Anti-Coercion Instrument after China boycotted Lithuanian goods in response to the opening of a Taiwanese Representative Office in Vilnius, but it has yet to use it. That same year, the G-7 announced a new Coordination Platform on Economic Coercion, which pledged members to warn each other and cooperate against shared economic threats, such as China’s nonmarket policies and economic coercion on critical minerals. But the platform contained no binding commitments and has largely been ignored.
These initiatives foundered from a lack of urgency and a reluctance among European countries to antagonize China, which is one of their largest trading partners. They were also constrained by disputes between European countries and the Biden administration over steel and aluminum tariffs and the large domestic subsidies in the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act. But Trump’s second-term policies have been the nail in the coffin. U.S. tariffs and threats to annex Greenland have rattled trust among American allies. Washington’s trade truce with Beijing has dispelled illusions that the transatlantic partners form a united front and made European partners doubt that the United States will come to their aid. Calls are indeed growing within Europe for de-risking and “digital sovereignty”—but from the United States, not China.
These calls will not be easy to quiet, even if Trump is followed by a president focused less on tariffs and more on building alliances. During the Biden administration, allies told U.S. officials that they would not commit to larger-scale economic coordination on shared challenges regarding China, Ukraine, or the Middle East because they were concerned that a future U.S. president could erase the progress. Europe’s concerns are well founded. As American politics has become increasingly polarized, more power has amassed in the executive branch. Congress, which historically provided ballast in U.S. foreign policy, has been absent. When Trump announced sweeping duties under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act against U.S. allies in April 2025, Congress did effectively nothing. When the Supreme Court ruled these tariffs as unconstitutional, the administration pivoted to other tariff authorities, and again, Congress stood by. Rebuilding trust will therefore require an institutional remedy that goes beyond communiqués and professions that “America is back.”
There is reason to think that the United States can repair its ties. The country still has a strong economic relationship with Europe. The value of cross-border mergers and acquisitions and investments across the Atlantic last year remained mostly normal, and total trade in goods and services between the United States and the EU increased by nearly six percent over the course of 2025. There is also little evidence a major economic rupture is coming. Despite frustrations with Washington in European capitals, European businesses want to maintain ties with the United States.
More important, Europe has finally awoken to the economic threat from China, because the surge of auto and industrial exports from China to Europe poses an existential challenge for the continent’s economic model. Chinese auto exports to Europe increased by 29 percent in 2025 and by over 60 percent year-over-year in 2026 as European auto exports to China have flatlined. Germany’s mighty auto industry alone lost 50,000 jobs in 2025. Even Volkswagen, which lobbied against the EU’s tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in 2024, has changed its tune. In July, its CEO all but urged the EU to extend tariffs to Chinese plug-in hybrids. Germany, which shed 74,000 industrial workers in non-auto sectors in 2025, has begun quietly identifying chokepoints it can use as leverage over China. Despite a provisional agreement with Beijing to curb Chinese hybrid vehicle exports in October, Brussels appears poised to unveil new measures against China on chemicals and machinery in the coming months as it finally grapples with the threat of Chinese industrial overcapacity.
These challenges will only get worse in the coming years and make Europe more likely to seek the United States’ help. And in Washington, the notion of a united Western front against Beijing has bipartisan resonance. As Kurt Campbell and Rush Doshi have recently argued in Foreign Affairs, even if the Trump administration continues to alienate some European partners, shared interests will keep them open to allied cooperation when the next administration comes.
At a port in Shenzhen, China, October 2025 Tingshu Wang / Reuters
When it does, the most important step will be terminating every tariff—issued pursuant to Section 232, Section 301, Section 338, or Section 201—and pending investigation against any ally that was imposed during the second Trump administration. This would present both a unilateral demonstration of good faith and an opening gambit for negotiations on an economic security alliance. It would be a decisive break from Trump’s tariff policy and a rejection of Biden’s halfway model, which mostly turned tariffs into quotas and suspensions. It would be both politically popular, considering Americans’ dismal view of tariffs, and good for the economy, as the removal of duties could lower prices and accelerate growth. And because Trump’s tariffs have all been enacted via executive action, they can also be terminated that way.
As part of this first phase, the White House should also pledge support to any ally facing Chinese coercion, by providing targeted economic assistance or access to relevant stockpiles, such as the rare earths the Trump administration has begun amassing in its U.S. Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve. If the president made good on such pledges, it would demonstrate concrete benefits to potential members and build confidence in the alliance’s viability.
These unilateral measures would set the table for a formal economic security treaty. That treaty’s foundation would include an economic mutual defense commitment, mimicking NATO’s Article 5, which would go a long way toward restoring Western escalation dominance over China and therefore defanging Beijing’s threats. Such a pledge would have both defensive and offensive components. For defense, members would commit to providing targeted allies with economic assistance, preferential market access, and access to stockpiles of critical goods. Offensively, members would respond to coercion against an ally by applying joint sanctions, tariffs, or export controls. The United States, the EU, and Japan should form the core of this alliance given their individual economic and strategic heft, but other like-minded partners, such as Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, should be welcome to join as well.
Collective economic defense could follow a path similar to NATO.
Ensuring the alliance’s longevity will require more than goodwill gestures carried out by executive action. The most durable approach would be a congressional-executive agreement backed by legislation, which would embed the alliance firmly in U.S. law and make it harder to unwind. Critically, this legislation should protect allies from the whims of future presidents. Over the years, Congress has delegated broad powers to the executive to impose tariffs for national security and other reasons—powers that recent administrations have used with reckless abandon. Congressional treaty legislation could codify the removal of these excessive tariffs and restrict any additional duties on alliance members unless approved by Congress. This self-limiting measure would give allies confidence that the bargain would survive changes of U.S. administrations. To address the possibility that novel legal theories could somehow be used by the executive branch in the future, the treaty legislation should also enact an automatic sunset after 60 days on any new duties on alliance members unless Congress affirmatively acts to retain them. Finally, the bill would pre-authorize rapid assistance to any ally facing foreign economic coercion, giving the executive the authority to honor the pact’s collective defense commitment.
These measures would be important not only to improve trust between governments but also between governments and the private sector. Firms make investment decisions based partly on whether they expect relations between countries to remain stable and predictable—often on a five- or ten-year time horizon, beyond any one U.S. presidential term. Today, in light of the transatlantic friction over trade and technology, many companies are debating whether to create separate operational and supply chain ecosystems for Europe and the United States. By constraining a future U.S. president’s ability to impose new tariffs on alliance members, an economic security pact would give companies confidence to build lasting economic links across the alliance system, even in the absence of a formal free-trade agreement.
Enacting ambitious legislation is always difficult, but there is reason to believe that U.S. lawmakers would be supportive of such an alliance. Chinese economic coercion is a bipartisan concern. Although some members of Congress may be wary of coming out against tariffs, the tool has become significantly less popular during Trump’s second term, and reclaiming congressional authority over tariff policy would serve Congress’s institutional interests. In a February survey by the Harris Poll, 72 percent of Americans agreed that Trump’s tariffs have had more of a negative than a positive impact, with 60 percent of Republicans agreeing that they have negatively impacted consumers. Tariffs on allies are especially unpopular: in an Ipsos poll conducted in August, Americans opposed placing additional tariffs on Canada by nearly three to one. Tariffs have also become closely associated with inflation. In an August poll conducted by the Council on Foreign Relations and Morning Consult, 75 percent of Americans reported being concerned about the price of food and groceries, and 83 percent of that group said that tariffs had increased those prices. With affordability now Americans’ number one concern, lawmakers have strong incentives to vote for legislation limiting tariffs.
The United States would have to lead the way for an economic security alliance, but just as important would be negotiations among potential members over the rules governing the pact itself. The agreement should spell out how collective defense would work in practice, specifying how allies can facilitate sharing commercial information and economic intelligence; who determines when economic coercion has occurred; and what kind of assistance, offensive and defensive, members can expect in such an event. If the alliance were successful in expanding its membership and scope, it could establish an independent secretariat to help it function, but the goal should be to make commitments credible without creating another sprawling international bureaucracy.
Collective economic defense would be just the starting point. Over time, the alliance could adapt to address a broader set of economic security challenges. On Chinese overcapacity, members could coordinate tariffs on the sectors most distorted by nonmarket practices such as subsidies and preferential financing, preventing Beijing from simply redirecting surplus exports from one allied market to another, or leverage a common baseline tariff on Chinese goods to compel Beijing to strengthen its undervalued currency. The same logic applies to export controls, which Western countries vary widely in applying. To break reliance on Chinese critical minerals, members could use the alliance to simplify the confusing set of international critical mineral initiatives underway by streamlining financing, making long-term purchase commitments, investing in processing, and building up stockpiles.
In this way, collective economic defense could follow a path similar to NATO. The North Atlantic alliance began with a relatively simple security guarantee that evolved into a cohesive military bloc: common institutions, shared planning, interoperable capabilities, and habits of cooperation that would have been difficult to create at the outset. An economic security alliance could evolve in much the same way. A credible promise of mutual defense would create the confidence needed for governments and firms to integrate more deeply over time.
Crisis has created opportunity for institution building in the past.
To be sure, an economic zone for the free world would be an ambitious undertaking, especially at a moment of unusually low trust between the United States and its allies. But the United States, Europe, and Japan do not need to agree on all matters of economic statecraft to build such a space, nor do they need to trust that future governments will always share the same priorities. What they need are institutions that allow them to cooperate despite those disagreements and that make their most important commitments durable enough to survive political change.
Moments of geopolitical rupture have provided fertile ground for institution building in the past. NATO emerged amid doubts about whether U.S. support would continue after World War II. In 1956, the Suez crisis badly strained U.S.-British relations, but in the years following, Washington and London rebuilt their partnership and established the 1958 Mutual Defense Agreement, which solidified nuclear cooperation and further bound the two countries together. The economic turmoil of the early 1970s, including the United States’ controversial exit from the Bretton Woods system and the Arab oil embargo, ended up pushing the major industrial democracies toward regular economic coordination that evolved into the G-7. In each case, crisis created opportunity.
Today, the hardest part for Washington will be accepting constraints on its freedom to act unilaterally. Presidents of both parties have long been wary of legislative checks on executive power out of fear that binding their hands would signal weakness. But if American power is constrained by predictable rules, allies will be more comfortable depending on it. If allies fear American economic power, they will hedge against it. Washington, in reserving the right to turn its economic weapons against its allies, will struggle to mobilize the collective weight of its alliances in markets, technology, and capital.
China’s divide-and-conquer strategy has capitalized on distrust within the U.S. alliance system. Restoring that trust will require Washington to make commitments that persist no matter who occupies the White House. The central wager of an economic security alliance is that the United States can gain leverage over China by surrendering some leverage over its allies. An economic zone for the free world can turn the tide against China, but only if the United States ties itself to the mast.

香港金管局使用代币化央行资金以 24/7 结算方式推进 Ensemble 项目 |中国劳工公告栏
星期一, 2 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版
HKMA 使用代币化央行资金推进 Ensemble 项目，进行 24/7 结算
香港金融管理局于 11 月 2 日宣布，Ensemble 项目的试点阶段 EnsembleTX 现在支持使用代币化央行货币进行代币化存款的 24/7 银行间结算。参与银行增至12家，行业先锋增至20家，标志着更广泛的行业参与
香港金融管理局（HKMA）于 11 月 2 日宣布，其 Ensemble 项目 EnsembleTX 的试点阶段已进入新篇章，支持使用代币化央行货币进行银行间代币化存款的 24/7 结算。参与银行数量已增至 12 家，行业先锋数量增至 20 家，反映出更广泛的行业参与。
新功能允许参与银行和行业先驱者在传统营业时间之外使用代币化央行货币进行代币化交易的实时结算，满足日益全球化和全天候数字金融市场的需求。
EnsembleTX于2025年11月推出，最初使用香港的实时支付结算系统进行代币化存款的银行间结算。它在受控试点环境中实现了涉及代币化存款和数字资产的真实交易，包括行业先驱使用参与银行提供的代币化存款进行企业资金管理和代币化货币市场基金交易。新功能旨在促进更大的交易量并探索更具影响力的代币化用例，以提供切实的利益并支持代币化市场的可持续发展。
展望未来，金管局将深化与证券及期货事务监察委员会（证监会）的合作，营造支持和协同的环境，进一步发展代币化金融生态系统和相关市场基础设施。
金管局行政总裁余伟文表示：“在短短两年内，Ensemble 项目已从实验和试点阶段进入推动香港代币化商业应用的新阶段。基础设施的快速稳定升级凸显了金管局对促进香港代币化生态系统发展的承诺。随着市场的发展，全球银行发行代币化存款的趋势日益明显。展望未来，我们预计代币化存款和数字资产的商业化将进一步加速。我们热切期待未来几年市场上出现更多创新想法，以进一步推进香港的代币化生态系统。”
证监会行政总裁梁凤仪表示：“使用代币化央行货币推出 24/7 银行间结算，是香港迈向更具可扩展性的代币化市场的重要一步。代币化存款将支持全天候交易，包括企业资金管理和牌照平台上代币化基金的二级市场交易，有助于增强市场流动性并支持投资者的风险管理需求。证监会将继续与金管局和市场参与者合作，将EnsembleTX的新功能投入实际应用，进一步推动香港的数字资产发展。

HKMA advances Ensemble project with 24/7 settlement using tokenised central bank money | China Labour Bulletin Board
Monday, 2 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
HKMA advances Ensemble project with 24/7 settlement using tokenised central bank money
Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced on 2 November that the Ensemble project's pilot phase EnsembleTX now supports 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenised deposits using tokenised central bank money. Participating banks have increased to 12 and industry pioneers to 20, marking broader industry enga
Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced on 2 November that the pilot phase of its Ensemble project, EnsembleTX, has entered a new chapter by supporting 24/7 settlement of interbank tokenised deposits using tokenised central bank money. The number of participating banks has increased to 12 and industry pioneers to 20, reflecting broader industry engagement.
The new function allows participating banks and industry pioneers to conduct real-time settlement of tokenised transactions using tokenised central bank money outside traditional operating hours, meeting the demands of an increasingly globalised and round-the-clock digital financial market.
EnsembleTX was launched in November 2025, initially using Hong Kong's real-time payment settlement system for interbank settlement of tokenised deposits. It enabled real transactions involving tokenised deposits and digital assets in a controlled pilot environment, including enterprise treasury management and tokenised money market fund transactions by industry pioneers using tokenised deposits provided by participating banks. The new function aims to facilitate larger transaction volumes and explore more impactful tokenisation use cases to deliver tangible benefits and support sustainable development of the tokenised market.
Looking ahead, HKMA will deepen cooperation with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) to create a supportive and synergistic environment to further develop the tokenised financial ecosystem and related market infrastructure.
HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said: 'In just two years, the Ensemble project has moved from experimentation and piloting to a new phase of driving commercial applications of tokenisation in Hong Kong. The swift and steady upgrade of infrastructure underscores the HKMA's commitment to fostering the development of Hong Kong's tokenisation ecosystem. As the market evolves, the trend of global banks issuing tokenised deposits is becoming increasingly evident. Looking ahead, we expect commercialisation of tokenised deposits and digital assets to accelerate further. We eagerly anticipate more innovative ideas from the market in the coming years to further advance Hong Kong's tokenisation ecosystem.'
SFC Chief Executive Julia Leung said: 'The introduction of 24/7 interbank settlement using tokenised central bank money is an important step towards a more scalable tokenised market in Hong Kong. Tokenised deposits will support round-the-clock transactions, including enterprise treasury management and secondary market trading of tokenised funds on licensed platforms, helping to enhance market liquidity and support investors' risk management needs. The SFC will continue to work with the HKMA and market participants to put the new functions of EnsembleTX into practical use and further advance Hong Kong's digital asset development.'

Ford launches a ‘privacy promise’ and explains how and why it uses customer data
3:00 AM PST · November 2, 2026
As Ford prepares to launch a new generation of connected cars, the automaker is making a public promise about how it will handle that information.
The company unveiled on Monday what it calls a “privacy promise” — an “explicit commitment” to keep customers’ vehicle data safe and give them control over what they share. Ford also launched a website designed to educate customers about how, where, and why the automakers uses their data, and to show them how to change those settings.
While those controls have existed for years now, Ford wants to communicate more clearly with its customers about them, especially ahead of the launch of new, more connected vehicles like the ones being built on its upcoming “universal electric vehicle” platform.
“I personally think that it’s super important for us to be making it very clear to our customers what our data practices are, and not only that, but making a commitment to them about it,” Ford’s chief privacy officer Kristin Jones said in an interview with TechCrunch. “I also see this as a great opportunity to educate our customers about how they share data.”
This new privacy push comes as automakers are making their cars increasingly connected. While some polling shows U.S. customers want the kinds of features enabled by this connectivity, such as remote start, navigation, and driver-assistance software, only 14% said they fully understand what data their vehicle collects.
That has left room for some companies to quietly sell that data to third parties — a practice that got General Motors in trouble with the Federal Trade Commission, and also resulted in a $220 million settlement with 36 states last week.
This lack of consumer awareness around data collection and sharing has also opened the door for other companies to market themselves as better stewards of customer data. Slate Auto, the EV startup backed by Jeff Bezos, has made that pitch ahead of the expected launch of its minimalist pickup truck later this year.
“We did a survey of 1,000 consumers, and 91% of them said that data privacy was a key consideration for them. Realistically, it’s not something they engage with every day, but they want to know that they’re, again, in control, and that they have access to the information they need there,” Jones said. “I wouldn’t comment on what our competitors are doing, or anything that’s sort of been in the news there, but certainly it’s something that people don’t trust companies to take care with their data, and we really want to make sure we’re building that trust relationship with them.”
Jones, who joined Ford in 2024 after nearly two decades of working on privacy in the legal, financial, and healthcare fields, said the effort to improve how the automaker communicates with customers about data sharing has been in the works for a while.
“It’s been a journey for, frankly, most of the time I’ve been at Ford,” she said.
Ford’s new website will feature a mix of content that explains what data the company collects, how it uses that information, and how customers can opt in or out.
Opting out of sharing some data will naturally make some modern features inaccessible, Jones said. For example, turning off “connected services” in a Ford vehicle will disable features like real-time navigation and the built-in access to roadside assistance.
But one of the goals of this “privacy promise” push is to better justify why Ford is asking for access to this data and make it clear that the information won’t be used for purposes such as targeted advertising.
Giving Ford access to data about a vehicle’s health, for instance, will provide an owner with better real-time information about whether their car needs maintenance. But it will also “support research and development for future technologies,” Jones said.
“We also do not share information about how our customers are driving their vehicles to data brokers,” Jones said. “I just want to kind of reiterate that we’re not in it to try and monetize data in some way. We’re trying to offer products and services that customers derive value from.”

# Thai Activist Sentenced to Additional Prison Term For Defaming Monarchy During 2020 Protest

Arnon Nampa, 42, now faces more than 34 years in prison for multiple breaches of Thailand’s strict lese-majeste law.

By [Sebastian Strangio](https://thediplomat.com/authors/sebastian-strangio/)

A Thai court has sentenced the political activist Arnon Nampa to an additional two years and eight months in prison for defaming the monarchy during a protest in 2020, bringing his total prison term to more than 34 years.

The 42-year-old has been in prison since 2023 on multiple charges under Thailand’s Article 112, commonly known as the lese-majeste law, which criminalizes criticisms of the Thai king or the royal family.

In a hearing on Friday at the Bangkok Criminal Court, Arnon and four other defendants – Wanwalee Thammasattaya, Phongsatorn Tancharoen, Promsorn Veerathamjaree, and Nawat Liangwattana – were sentenced to two years and eight months in prison on a fresh count of lese majeste, the AFP news agency [reported](https://www.arabnews.com/world/thailand-extends-activists-jail-term-to-more-than-34-years-3008982).

According to a [report](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40072928) in Thailand’s The Nation newspaper, the charges stem from a 2020 protest that Arnon participated in front of the Siam Commercial Bank headquarters. During the protest, the defendants took turns delivering speeches calling “for the resignation of then prime minister General Prayut Chan-o-cha, constitutional amendments, and reform of the monarchy.”

Arnon’s lawyer Krisadang Nutcharut [told AFP](https://www.arabnews.com/world/thailand-extends-activists-jail-term-to-more-than-34-years-3008982) that Arnon was calling for increased transparency over a transfer of shares in Siam Commercial Bank, Thailand’s oldest bank, from the Crown Property Bureau. King Vajiralongkorn is the largest shareholder in SCBx, the bank’s parent company.

The defendants attempted to argue that their conduct was protected by the constitutional right to assembly. However, the judges ruled that the remarks exceeded lawful limits and insulted and defamed the monarchy. The Court initially sentenced each of them to four years in prison, which was [reduced](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40072928) to two years and eight months each, stating that their testimony “was of some assistance to the proceedings.”

Arnon was one of the main leaders of the campaign of youth-dominated protests that erupted in the first half of 2020, after the court-ordered dissolution of the progressive Future Forward Party. Before they petered out in 2021, due to a combination of COVID-19 restrictions and state repression, the protests were notable for breaching the taboo on open discussion of the monarchy and its political role.

Thailand’s conservative establishment responded by initiating scores of lese-majeste complaints against the main leaders of the protest movement. Si

content: 作者：王五四  2026-10-28 世界上最容易受伤的情感，大概就是中国人民的感情了，每隔一段时间就要被伤害几次。这次伤害中国人民感情的是足球明星姆巴佩。我发现中国人民的感情，只有在足球这个领域是坚强的，或者说是正常的，你再怎么射，也很难伤害到我。所以，这次姆巴佩伤害中国人民的情感，不是因为射进了中国队多少球，他还没这个资格，因为近些年中国队还没资格进入世界杯。 懂球帝称，姆巴佩是因为言论伤害了中国人民的感情，而这个言论是他们无法翻译的。所以至今，很多中国人民都不知道姆巴佩为何伤害了中国人民的感情，所以，能不能这么说，其实很多中国人民的感情并没有受到伤害，没有翻译，就没伤害，无欲则刚，无知也刚。 国内的媒体铺天盖地的指责姆巴佩对中国人民感情的伤害，义正言辞的要求他道歉和反思，但却没有一家媒体敢说明缘由所在，这种行为其实很可笑，很给中国人民丢脸，很伤害中国人民的情感。试想一下，如果姆巴佩说的是中国没有新闻自由呢？你们这样搞不正好自证了吗？这才是吃人民的饭砸人民的锅。 在中国人民还一头雾水时，姆巴佩又道歉了，这太像网上的一个段子了，有人因为造谣自己因造谣而被拘留十五天而被拘留十五天。我相信，在很大一片世界里，是这样一个状况，道歉者不知为何道歉，被伤害者不知因何受伤，但总之，世界再次大团结。 在姆巴佩被媒体讨伐时，很多品牌第一时间官宣跟他解约，包括蒙牛。其实姆巴佩当初跟这个牌子签约代言时，我的情感就被伤害了，因为蒙牛的奶在三聚氰胺毒奶时代就伤害了中国人民的身体，2008年三聚氰胺事件期间，它的CFO姚同山在香港新闻发布会上称“供港产品没问题，因使用规模化牧场原奶，问题几率比内地少”，并明确表示“香港与内地产品从原料到生产线均不同”，一国两奶，这才是极大伤害了中国人民的感情。 中国人民的感情时而强大，时而弱不经风，当面对各种食品安全问题，环境问题，医疗问题，教育问题，养老问题，就业问题时，这些问题反而伤害不了中国人民的感情，它们甚至都伤害了中国人民的身体了，但人民的情绪依然稳定，这大概是几十年来维稳工作的成绩。不论遇到什么灾难结果，我们得到的通报结果往往是受难家属“情绪稳定”。 而另外一方面，中国人民的情绪又特别不稳定，情感又特别容易受到伤害，不论国外的谁说了句什么话，中国人民自己都没听到，甚至打听都打听不到，但它就是伤害了中国人民的感情。当我们的孩子喝着三鹿蒙牛三聚氰胺毒奶时，当我们吃着林可霉素超标37.5倍的双汇火腿肠时，没人说这些企业和它们的产品伤害了中国人民的身体和感情，反而是这些事被外边的媒体揪出来时，涉事企业反咬一口说西方媒体伤害了中国人民的感情，我不得不怀疑，“中国人民的感情”病了，是身体上的病，也是精神上的病。 “中国人民的感情”和“遇难者家属的情绪”是两个很有意思的词，是两个早就注定了属性的词，感情必须激动，情绪必须稳定。灾难现场的家属于悲痛中被要求“情绪稳定”，这其实是在说：你的痛苦可以存在，但必须保持安静。而“中国人民的感情”恰恰相反——你可以对外界无感，但必须表演激动。同一个主体，被要求同时具备两种截然相反的情感模式，这本身就说明问题不在于“感情”本身，而在于感情被谁定义、被谁调度，时间久了，精神能不出问题吗？ 像之前说的食品安全、环境污染、医疗教育养老这些，它们有一个共同点：责任链条清晰可追溯。如果允许这些议题充分发酵，矛头会指向具体的制度环节、监管缺位、权力失职。而被外国和外国人伤害情感的民族主义叙事，责任在外，情绪出口向外，加以引导，一举两得，所以这不是中国人民的感情脆弱，而是某些感情被迫营业，某些感情被要求压抑。 中国人民的感情很容易被伤害这件事，其实是把一种复杂判断用强大外力压缩成了一个道德判断。一旦某件事被贴上“伤害中国人民感情”的标签，公共讨论空间就被迅速关闭，谁再追问事实、边界或理性探讨，谁就可能被反扣“不爱国”“洗地”“崇洋媚外”的帽子。 中国人民的感情，当然要尊重，“攘外必先安内”，从内部开始就得认真尊重，不能自己内部不尊重，却强烈要求洋人尊重，更不能被借题发挥和裹挟。中国人民的感情，最该被认真对待，也最该被谨慎使用，它适合用来守住内部的底线，却不应被当成对外的万能锤子，见什么都敲。 尊重中国人民的感情，那就得让中国人民有知情权，不要让中国人民被伤害了半天，却还不知道是如何被伤害的，更不能说一句无法翻译就了事。任何人都不应该怕中国人民自由地表达，也不应该怕西方人议论中国，更没必要怕西方人的议论会伤害中国人民的感情，毛曾说过，让人讲话，天塌不下来。他还强调，“让人讲话”决不是什么“天塌”的事，而是“天大”的事，“不怕说错话，就怕不说话”，更怕不让人说话，不让人说话才是天塌了。 民族主义叙事说好听点就像碗热水，不管什么病，他们都告诉你，多喝热水。说难听点就是鸡血，先燥起来再说，它让人迷失自我，就像当年有人组织了包括中学生在内的20万人大会要批判爱因斯坦的相对论。就像当年有人批判莫扎特的音乐，“资产阶级当然可以认为莫扎特作品中具有明朗、健康的情调。但是，我们无产阶级却清楚地知道，这种情调和《白毛女》第七场“太阳出来了”的大合唱洋溢着的开朗、奔放的情感，是根本不能相提并论的。” 这就是喝热水和打鸡血民族主义叙事效果，这些话之所以显得“无知”，并不是因为群众一定愚蠢，而是因为当时的批判机制不允许真正的知识讨论。科学问题被替换成政治标签，专业判断被发动的情绪取代，最后就出现了这种结果：越不懂，越敢判，越说不清，越要上纲上线。 既然你不肯告诉中国人民姆巴佩是如何伤害中国人民感情的，那么中国人民就没必要接受姆巴佩的道歉，当然我们也无处接受，那么伤害中国人民感情的必定另有他人。

title: Oshkosh steps into large UAS space with new Grid Aero partnership
zh_title: 奥什科什与 Grid Aero 建立新合作伙伴关系，进军大型无人机领域
summary: 奥什科什与 Grid Aero 建立新合作伙伴关系，进军大型无人机领域——突破防御 奥什科什防务公司 (Oshkosh Defense) 正在与自主飞机公司 Grid Aero 建立新的合作伙伴关系。 （奥什科什防务公司、Grid Aero）华盛顿——周一宣布，奥什科什防务公司正在与自主飞机公司 Grid Aero 合作，旨在扩大后者的 Lifter 无人机的生产规模。此次合作正值五角大楼正在推动经济实惠的第 4 组和第 5 组无人自主系统 (UAS)（例如 Grid Aero 的 Lifter，其设计于去年 8 月推出）时达成。
content:
奥什科什与 Grid Aero 建立新合作伙伴关系，进军大型无人机领域 - Breaking Defense
奥什科什防务公司 (Oshkosh Defense) 正在与自主飞机公司 Grid Aero 建立新的合作伙伴关系。 （奥什科什防御、Grid Aero）
华盛顿——周一宣布，奥什科什防务公司正在与自主飞机公司 Grid Aero 合作，旨在扩大后者的 Lifter 无人机的生产规模。
此次合作正值五角大楼正在推动经济实惠的第 4 组和第 5 组无人自主系统 (UAS)（例如 Grid Aero 的 Lifter，其设计于去年 8 月公布）进行大规模生产，并且可以批量购买。
奥什科什防务公司首席增长官洛根琼斯在今天的一份声明中表示：“这种合作伙伴关系代表了国防创新的新模式，将硅谷的变革性技术开发与中西部无与伦比的制造能力结合在一起。” “Grid Aero 带来了尖端的自主飞机创新，而 Oshkosh 则带来了使其规模化的工业能力。我们将共同通过美国创新和美国制造来满足关键的国防需求。”
具体来说，根据奥什科什的新闻稿，两家公司计划合作“可制造性设计、生产规划、供应链优化，并最终大规模制造 Lifter 飞机”。
Grid Aero 首席执行官阿瑟·杜布瓦 (Arthur Dubois) 表示，Lifter 飞机的设计目的是运输“几千磅”重量、飞行“几千英里”，并承担从情报、监视和侦察 (ISR) 到运输货物等各种任务。
杜波依斯告诉 Breaking Defense：“我们的目标是尽可能实现有效载荷集成系统的模块化，无论是用于货物、ISR 还是其他用途。” “我不会告诉你我们是为了任何一个特定目的而设计它。我们将它设计成就像模块化皮卡车一样，你知道它上面可以安装任何东西。”
杜波依斯表示，最终目标是到 2030 年代初生产数百架（如果不是数千架）此类飞机。
赞助帖子，陆战
导弹和雷达需要的不仅仅是需求——它们需要制造能力
扩大制造能力对于生产导弹、雷达和发射系统至关重要。
Dubois 估计目前正在建造或正在制作的各种 Lifter 原型还需要 6 到 12 个月的测试时间。他表示，预计两家公司将在大约一年内在奥什科什推出一条试点生产线。
Dubois 表示，Grid Aero 将与 Oshkosh 共同讨论一些设计变更，“将平台重新设计到下一个版本”。即便如此，杜波依斯表示，他预计飞机将在很大程度上保持其原始形状，尽管用于制造飞机的零件可能会发生一些变化。
“这次合作的开始是我们重新审视机身的设计，并与奥什科什的供应链团队合作，研究我们实际上可以购买这些数量的零件，研究哪些方法实际上可以按照我们想要的速度工作，研究奥什科什的员工知道如何做才能更好地将其融入到设计中，”杜布瓦说。
奥什科什防务公司以制造军用车辆而闻名，其中包括联合轻型战术车辆。 Grid Aero 于 2025 年 8 月崭露头角，总部位于加利福尼亚州。

Oshkosh steps into large UAS space with new Grid Aero partnership - Breaking Defense
Oshkosh Defense is teaming up with autonomous aircraft company Grid Aero in a new partnership. (Oshkosh Defense, Grid Aero)
WASHINGTON — Oshkosh Defense is teaming up with autonomous aircraft firm Grid Aero, in a partnership aimed at scaling up production on the latter’s Lifter drone, the companies announced Monday.
The partnership comes as the Pentagon is pushing for affordable Group 4 and 5 unmanned autonomous systems (UAS) — like Grid Aero’s Lifter, the design of which was unveiled last August — that are produced at scale and that it can purchase in bulk.
“This partnership represents a new model for defense innovation, bringing Silicon Valley’s transformative technology development together with the Midwest’s unmatched manufacturing capability,” Logan Jones, chief growth officer of Oshkosh Defense, said in a statement today. “Grid Aero brings cutting-edge autonomous aircraft innovation, and Oshkosh brings the industrial capability to make it real at scale. Together, we’re addressing critical defense needs with American innovation and American manufacturing.”
Specifically, the two companies plan to team up on “design for manufacturability, production planning, supply chain optimization, and ultimately building Lifter aircraft at scale,” according to an Oshkosh news release.
Arthur Dubois, CEO of Grid Aero, said the Lifter aircraft is designed to haul a “few” thousand pounds, for a “few” thousand miles, and take on a variety of mission sets, ranging from intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), to hauling cargo.
“Our objective is to be as modular as we can with the payload integration systems, whether it’s for cargo, ISR, even other purposes,” Dubois told Breaking Defense. “I’m not going to tell you that we’re designing it for any one specific purpose. We’re designing it to be just like modular pickup truck that you know can have anything mounted on top of it.”
Ultimately, the goal is to produce hundreds, if not thousands, of these aircraft by the early 2030s, according to Dubois.

Missiles and radar need more than demand – they need manufacturing capacity
Expanding manufacturing capacity is critical to producing missiles, radars, and launch systems.
Dubois estimated there are another six to 12 months of testing for the variety of Lifter prototypes that are being built or are in the works at the moment. In roughly a year, he said he expects that the two companies will launch a pilot line at Oshkosh.
Grid Aero will hash out some design alterations with Oshkosh as they work in tandem to “redesign the platform into its next iteration,” Dubois said. Even so, Dubois said he expects the aircraft to largely maintain its original shape — although there may be some changes related to the parts used to build the aircraft.
“The start of this collaboration is us revisiting the design of the airframe, and working with Oshkosh’s team on supply chain, working on what parts we can actually buy in those volumes, working on what methods actually would work at the the kind of rates we want to build at, working on what Oshkosh’s workforce knows how to do to better integrate that into the design,” Dubois said.
Oshkosh Defense is known for building military vehicles, including Joint Light Tactical Vehicles. Grid Aero emerged from stealth in August 2025, and is based in California.

title: Marine Force-Southeast Asia Will Maintain Continuous Presence in the Philippines
zh_title: 东南亚海军陆战队将继续在菲律宾保持存在
summary: 美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北部海空炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换营业额。 MR
content:
美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北部海空炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换。MRF-SEA 最初是一支为期六个月的轮换部队，从 10 月到 3 月部署到该地区，但其任务在 4 月延长。应菲律宾政府邀请，该部队目前在菲律宾持续驻扎，以继续与菲律宾军方合作。 MRF-SEA 是在第一海军陆战队远征军支持下作战的两支轮换部队之一，另一支是海军陆战队轮换部队-达尔文。与作为海军陆战队空地特遣部队部署的 MRF-D 不同，MRF-SEA 部署为可扩展的特遣部队，其指挥总部是常设组成部分。其他海军陆战队单位将根据需要进行分配。我们。
2026 年 6 月 24 日，为支持 MRF-SEA 而部署的第三濒海战斗队、海军陆战队第三临海团、海军陆战队第三师的海军陆战队士兵和海军陆战队第四旅的菲律宾海军陆战队士兵，在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊特巴亚特的海上关键地形安全行动期间，在地形巡逻的同时参加城市地形军事行动，以支持 KAMANDAG 10。美国海军陆战队照片轮换前延期后，MRF-SEA 的指挥部门将根据预定活动的地点在东南亚国家之间移动。自四月份以来，指挥部门一直驻扎在菲律宾。目前的部署是 MRF-SEA 的第六次迭代。轮换部署于 2022 年开始。根据海军陆战队的一份新闻稿，该部队的存在旨在加强联合战备和美菲联盟，每次轮换都建立在之前部队的关系和经验教训的基础上，MRF-SEA 称之为“有目的的存在”。 “我们的目标从来都不是简单地出现在菲律宾，”即将卸任的 MRF-SEA 轮换指挥官罗伯特·邦恩 (Robert Bunn) 上校说道。 “存在必须有目的。与我们的菲律宾盟友一起进行的每一次演习、计划会议和重复都是一个机会，让我们变得更加具有互操作性、响应能力和能力，并在每次活动中逐渐变得更好。
下一次轮换现在有机会吸取这些教训和关系，推动联盟向前迈进一步。”之前的 MRF-SEA 轮换中，该部队在“肩并肩 26”演习、“卡曼达格 10”演习以及通过群岛海岸防御连续体 (ACDC) 进行的一系列双边活动期间与菲律宾军队一起进行了训练。该连续体在主要演习之间提供了反复训练，使美国和菲律宾部队能够将一次活动中的经验教训应用到下一次活动中。 ACDC是一系列双边训练活动和主题专家交流，支持菲律宾海军陆战队的现代化努力和菲律宾海军陆战队的群岛海岸防御概念，同时加强美国和菲律宾军队之间的联合战备。

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Marine Corps Cpl. Antwon Brooks, a fire support Marine with Air Naval Gunfire Liaison Company Detachment – North, Marine Rotational Force – Southeast Asia, I Marine Expeditionary Force, conducts fire support team training alongside Philippine marines with 4th Marine Brigade, Philippine Marine Corps, during Archipelagic Coastal Defense Continuum 26.4 in Bojeador, Philippines, Aug. 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Marine Rotational Force-Southeast Asia is now on its second continuous rotation to the Philippines, the service announced last week. MRF-SEA held a rotation turnover on Oct. 26. MRF-SEA originally began as a six-month rotational force that deployed to the region from October to March but its mission was extended in April . The force is now providing a continuous presence in the Philippines at the invitation of the country’s government to continue cooperation with its military. MRF-SEA is one of two rotational forces operating under the aegis of I Marine Expeditionary Force, with the other being Marine Rotational Force-Darwin. Unlike MRF-D, which deploys as a Marine Air-Ground Task Force, MRF-SEA deploys as a scalable task force with its command headquarters being the permanent component. Other Marine units are assigned as and when required. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, which deployed to support MRF-SEA, and Philippine marines assigned to 4th Marine Brigade, patrol through terrain while participating in military operations in urban terrain training during maritime key terrain security operations in support of KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes islands, Philippines, June 24, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Before the rotation extension, the command element of the MRF-SEA would move between Southeast Asian countries based on where scheduled activities would take place. Since April, the command element has been based in the Philippines The current deployment is the sixth iteration of MRF-SEA. The rotational deployment began in 2022. The unit’s presence is designed to strengthen combined readiness and the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, according to a Marine Corps news release, with each rotation building on the relationships and lessons of the force before in an approach MRF-SEA calls “presence with purpose.” “Our goal was never simply to be present in the Philippines,” said Col. Robert Bunn, commanding officer of the outgoing MRF-SEA rotation. “Presence has to have purpose. Every exercise, planning session and repetition alongside our Philippine allies was an opportunity to become more interoperable, responsive and capable together, progressively getting better with each event. The next rotation now has the opportunity to take those lessons and relationships to move the alliance another step forward.” The previous rotation of MRF-SEA saw the force train alongside Philippine troops during Balikatan 26, KAMANDAG 10 and a series of bilateral events through the Archipelagic Coastal Defense Continuum (ACDC). The continuum provided recurring training between major exercises, allowing U.S. and Philippine forces to apply lessons from one event to the next. ACDC is is a series of bilateral training activities and subject matter expert exchanges that support Philippine Marine Corps modernization efforts and the Philippine Marine Corps’ Archipelagic Coastal Defense Concept along with strengthening combined readiness between U.S. and Philippine forces Training throughout the previous MRF-SEA rotation included command and control, sensing, fires integration, maritime domain awareness, aviation, communications and unmanned systems. Marines also tested how forces and equipment could move, communicate and operate across the Philippines’ distributed and archipelagic terrain. This included testing the mobility of the AN/TPS-80 Ground/Air Task-Oriented Radar as part of ACDC training and movement of the Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System (NMESIS) and Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) from ports to distributed exercise locations as part of KAMANDAG 10. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Anti-Air Battalion, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, drive a Marine Air Defense Integrated System off a Philippine surface connector in support of maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Calayan, Philippines, June 22, 2026. US Marine Corps photo The incoming rotation will continue the progression of the U.S.-Philippine partnership through ACDC and Exercise Balikatan 27, according to the release. Training will continue to focus on operating across distributed and archipelagic terrain, strengthening the ability of U.S. and Philippine forces to coordinate, maneuver and sustain operations across geographically dispersed locations. Marines and sailors will also continue bilateral humanitarian assistance, disaster response and crisis response training. “Our Marines and sailors are inheriting more than a mission, they are inheriting momentum,” said Col. Coby Moran, commanding officer of the incoming MRF-SEA rotation. “We will build on the relationships, lessons and interoperability developed by the Marines and sailors before us and continue working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Philippine allies.” Moran previously operated in the Philippines, leading a I MEF technical assistance and advisory team in April that oversaw a maritime prepositioning force offload at the Port of Cagayan de Oro, Mindanao, Philippines. The event was the first MPF offload at Mindanao, according to a Marine Corps news release at the time . The offload saw roll-on/roll-off cargo ship USNS Sgt. William W. Seay (T-AKR-302) transport vehicles and equipment to I MEF, which was preparing for Exercise Balikatan 26 in the Philippines. “MPF operations are a unique capability of the Marine Corps,” said Moran in the release. “They allow us to deliver capabilities anywhere in the world, providing critical combat power to Marine air-ground task force commanders.” The Marine Corps has not disclosed whether MRF-SEA will now only focus on the Philippines or whether it will continue leading Marine Corps engagement and activities with other countries in the region alongside its activities in the Philippines.

When Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee announced the resignation of Housing Secretary Winnie Ho over the Wang Fuk Court fire, a bereaved family member questioned why only one minister had been made to bear political responsibility. Yip Ka-kui, who lost his wife in the disaster, described the government’s approach as accountability calculated with nanometer precision. “All the secretaries for the departments named should step down,” he said.

When there is credit to claim, Yip observed, ministers take their share. When things go wrong, the responsibility falls on those working beneath them.

His criticism exposed a fundamental problem with Hong Kong’s response to the fire that killed 168 people in November 2025. Eleven months after the tragedy, the government has offered apologies, a ministerial resignation, investigations into dozens of civil servants, and extensive proposals for bureaucratic reform. Yet the authority to determine who should be held politically responsible, and what consequences they should face, remains firmly in the hands of the government itself.

The [independent committee’s findings](https://www.ic-wangfukcourtfire.gov.hk/pdf/docs/Closing-Submissions-of-Counsel-for-the-Independent-Committee.pdf) were unequivocal. Residents had raised “numerous complaints and enquiries about fire safety concerns at Wang Fuk Court,” while government departments neglected warnings, failed to exercise “real supervision,” and allowed dangerous construction practices – like “the extensive use of foam boards to cover all windows” – to continue. The report identified serious regulatory failures involving the Housing Bureau’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU), the Buildings Department, the Fire Services Department, and the Labor Department.

In explaining Ho’s resignation, Lee pointed to the Housing Bureau’s oversight of the ICU, while stressing that she had committed no personal wrongdoing. He described Ho’s departure as his political decision, made after considering departmental responsibilities and other factors. Yet he provided no clear standard explaining why failures within the Housing Bureau warranted its minister’s resignation, while those involving other departments did not produce equivalent consequences.

Development Secretary Bernadette Linn, whose bureau oversees the Buildings Department, acknowledged having considered resigning. She nevertheless compared the chief executive to the captain of a ship, explaining that, as a member of his “crew,” she was obliged to follow his instructions. Labor and Welfare Secretary Chris Sun similarly stressed that politically appointed officials must answer to the chief executive, maintain team spirit, and demonstrate an awareness of the broader interests of the administration. content:
西班牙 Abenójar Tungsten (LON: ABT) 周五在伦敦证券交易所首次亮相，股价上涨，此前该公司在该市自 2018 年以来最大规模的矿业首次公开募股中筹集了 1.7 亿欧元（1.9 亿美元）。周二，当有条件交易开始时，该公司将 IPO 定价为每股 110 便士。周五午后交易中，该股上涨近 3%，至 105 便士，仍低于发行价。 “随着我们加入伦敦证券交易所主要市场，今天对 ABT 来说是一个真正重要的里程碑，”首席执行官 Gonzalo García San Miguel 在一份声明中表示。此次上市之际，西方政府正在寻求确保钨的供应，钨是一种用于国防系统、航空航天部件、工业切削工具和电子产品的重要矿物。中国主导着全球生产和加工，使得新的欧洲来源对该地区的供应安全变得越来越重要。战略供应 Abenójar 正在西班牙中部开发 El Moto 项目，该项目被描述为世界上最大、品位最高的未开发钨矿床之一。加西亚·圣米格尔表示，该矿及其规划中的加工设施均已被欧盟指定为战略项目。建设正在进行中，预计将于 2029 年第一季度实现首次商业生产。该公司还处于开发一座用于提炼矿山钨精矿的加工厂的早期阶段。 El Moto 钨项目。 （图片由 Abenójar Tungsten 提供。
）“我们的投资者将资金委托给我们有一个明确的目的：建造这座矿山，”加西亚·圣米格尔说。“而这正是我们打算做的。”这位首席执行官表示，伦敦是上市的自然选择，因为这里集中了有能力支持公司长期发展计划的专业矿业投资者。此次发行是自哈萨克斯坦铀生产商 Kazatomprom 在 2018 年通过全球存托凭证上市筹集 3.11 亿英镑（4.17 亿美元）以来该市规模最大的一次矿业上市。阿贝诺哈尔的市值为 5.22 亿英镑，正在接近可能纳入 FTSE 250 指数所需的规模，尽管其成员身份还取决于其他资格标准。发展重点 此次 IPO 标志着 Abenójar 在经过 14 年的投资和开发工作后的过渡，将 El Moto 从勘探前景推进到建设中的矿山。加西亚·圣米格尔说：“今天不是我们旅程的终点​​，而是新篇章的开始。” “IPO 本身并不是目的。”专栏：欧洲需要关键矿物，而不是矿山该公司现在必须按其建设计划交付并完成将矿藏投入商业生产所需的加工基础设施。 2029 年目标的实现将取决于未来两年这些计划的执行情况。
García San Miguel 表示，El Moto 可能成为欧洲最重要的钨矿产地之一，同时为阿贝诺哈尔和周边卡斯蒂利亚-拉曼恰地区创造就业机会和长期经济机会。BMO Capital Markets 和 Peel Hunt 与德意志银行一起担任联合保荐人和联合全球协调人，而 Canaccord Genuity 则担任联合账簿管理人。

【原文 English Original】
Shares in Spain’s Abenójar Tungsten (LON: ABT) gained on their London Stock Exchange debut Friday after the company raised €170 million ($190 million) in the city’s largest mining initial public offering since 2018. The company priced its IPO at 110 pence per share Tuesday, when conditional trading began. The shares rose almost 3% to 105 pence in early-afternoon trading Friday, remaining below its offering price. “Today marks a truly significant milestone for ABT as we join the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange,” CEO Gonzalo García San Miguel said in a statement .  The flotation comes as Western governments seek to secure supplies of tungsten, a critical mineral used in defence systems, aerospace components, industrial cutting tools and electronics. China dominates global production and processing, making new European sources increasingly important to the region’s supply security. Strategic supply Abenójar is developing the El Moto project in central Spain , which it describes as one of the world’s largest and highest-grade undeveloped tungsten deposits. Both the mine and its planned processing facility have been designated strategic projects by the European Union, García San Miguel said. Construction is underway, with first commercial production targeted for the first quarter of 2029. The company is also in the early stages of developing a processing plant to refine tungsten concentrate from the mine. El Moto tungsten project. ( Image courtesy of Abenójar Tungsten. ) “Our investors have entrusted us with their capital for one clear purpose: to build this mine,” García San Miguel said. “And that is exactly what we intend to do.” The CEO said London was the natural choice for the listing because of its concentration of specialist mining investors capable of supporting the company’s long-term development plans. The offering was the city’s biggest mining flotation by funds raised since Kazakhstan’s uranium producer Kazatomprom raised £311 million ($417 million) through a listing of global depositary receipts in 2018 . With a market capitalization of £522 million, Abenójar is approaching the size required for potential inclusion in the FTSE 250 index, although membership also depends on other eligibility criteria. Development priorities The IPO marks a transition for Abenójar after 14 years of investment and development work to advance El Moto from an exploration prospect into a mine under construction. “Today is not the end of our journey, it is the beginning of a new chapter,” García San Miguel said. “The IPO is not an end in itself.” Op-Ed: Europe wants critical minerals, just not the mines The company must now deliver on its construction schedule and complete the processing infrastructure needed to bring the deposit into commercial production. Meeting its 2029 target will depend on executing those plans over the next two years. García San Miguel said El Moto could become one of Europe’s most important tungsten sources while generating jobs and long-term economic opportunities in Abenójar and the surrounding Castilla-La Mancha region. BMO Capital Markets and Peel Hunt acted as joint sponsors and joint global coordinators alongside Deutsche Bank, while Canaccord Genuity served as joint bookrunner.

title: China-backed threat group used agentic AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets in 11 days
zh_title: 中国支持的威胁组织使用代理人工智能渗透测试工具在 11 天内入侵了 140 个敏感目标
summary: 据 CrowdStrike 称，一个中国国家支持的威胁组织正在使用 ARTEX（自动化代理 AI 渗透测试框架）在一场活动中取得了惊人的速度、规模和成功，该活动已在 11 天内入侵了约 140 个敏感目标。该安全公司在周四的威胁报告中表示，自 10 月 17 日以来，CrowdStrike 追踪的这个名为 Vapor Panda 的威胁组织已针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。目标和已确认的受害者包括外交部、欧洲国家总统府和总理办公室、国防和情报机构
content:
据 CrowdStrike 称，一个中国国家支持的威胁组织正在使用 ARTEX（自动化代理 AI 渗透测试框架）在一场活动中取得了惊人的速度、规模和成功，该活动已在 11 天内入侵了约 140 个敏感目标。该安全公司在周四的威胁报告中表示，自 10 月 17 日以来，CrowdStrike 追踪的这个名为 Vapor Panda 的威胁组织已针对至少 14 个国家的 200 多个组织。目标和已确认的受害者包括外交部、欧洲国家总统府和总理办公室、国防和情报机构；制药、半导体、国防、核能和金融领域的 19 个美国组织；以及美国、比利时和菲律宾的电信提供商。 CrowdStrike 告诉 Cyber​​Scoop，大约 70% 的 Vapor Panda 目标已被确认受到损害，或者有证据表明有一定程度的成功入侵的信心。 Vapor Panda 将 ARTEX 与 DeepSeek 配合使用，使其能够以惊人的速度完成更多任务（请求每 10 秒发生一次），并同时追求多个攻击路径。 CrowdStrike 反对手行动高级副总裁 Adam Meyers 告诉 Cyber​​Scoop：“这是我们第一次看到如此规模的代理对手民族国家威胁行为体，不幸的是，我认为我们可能会看到更多这种情况。”
CrowdStrike 在过去 15 年中跟踪的键盘操作活动通常每小时涉及多达 40 个命令。“现在，有了 ARTEX，我们可以看到每小时超过 1,500 个命令，”Meyers 说。他补充道：“如果你将目标分散到 200 个目标中，那么他们只需花费很少的成本即可开展大规模剥削活动并放弃网络销售。” “他们可以在更快的时间内击中更多目标。” Vapor Panda 的广泛访问活动仍然活跃，目标是国防、司法、金融和外交等领域的智囊团和政府机构。迈耶斯说：“我将其描述为一项多元化的行动任务，往往侧重于北京认为具有经济或政治重要性的部门和地区。” Vapor Panda 发起的活动与本月早些时候 Storm-0940 发起的 Microsoft Threat Intelligence ARTEX 活动不同，其中包括针对 ConnectWise 客户的供应链攻击。迈耶斯说，人工智能的对抗性使用相对较新，但也很快成为新常态。 “我们正在争先恐后，因为我们看到了太多这样的代理对手。”用于恶意目的的代理人工智能的使用量逐月以近三倍的速度增长。 CrowdStrike 在 9 月份观察到大约 45 起代理攻击，到 10 月份已经达到 126 起，并且还在不断攀升。
迈耶斯表示，代理人工智能的对抗性使用并不是一个棘手的问题，而是再次提醒人们，组织需要了解其端点、身份和跨域能力。这些攻击并没有展示任何新内容，“只是以我们不习惯的速度和规模进行攻击，”他说。 “这并不是绝望，但你必须采取行动。你不能把头埋在沙子里。”这个由中国支持的威胁组织使用代理人工智能渗透测试工具在 11 天内入侵了 140 个敏感目标，该组织首先出现在 Cyber​​Scoop 上。

【原文 English Original】
A China state-backed threat group is using ARTEX, the automated agentic AI penetration testing framework, to achieve remarkable speed, scale and success in a campaign that already compromised about 140 sensitive targets in 11 days, according to CrowdStrike.  The threat group, which CrowdStrike tracks as Vapor Panda, targeted more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries since Oct. 17, the security company said in a threat report Thursday. Targets and confirmed victims include foreign ministries, a European country’s presidency and prime minister’s office, defense and intelligence agencies; 19 U.S.-based organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial sectors; and telecom providers in the United States, Belgium and the Philippines.  CrowdStrike told CyberScoop about 70% of Vapor Panda’s targets were confirmed compromised or had evidence indicating moderate confidence of a successful intrusion.  Vapor Panda’s use of ARTEX, paired with DeepSeek, allowed it to accomplish more tasks with shocking speed — requests occurring as often as every 10 seconds — and pursue multiple attack paths concurrently.  “This is the first time that we’re seeing an agentic adversary nation-state threat actor at this scale, and I think that this is probably, unfortunately, something we’ll see more of,” Adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at CrowdStrike, told CyberScoop. Hands-on-keyboard activity tracked by CrowdStrike for the past 15 years typically involved up to 40 commands per hour. “Now, with ARTEX, we could see it exceed 1,500 commands an hour,” Meyers said. “If you diversify that across 200 targets, it costs them very little to run a mass-exploitation campaign and drop a websell,” he added. “They can hit more targets in a faster period of time.” Vapor Panda’s broad-access campaign, which remains active, has targeted think tanks and government agencies spanning defense, justice, finance and diplomacy. “I would characterize it as a diverse operational mission that tends to focus on sectors and geographies that Beijing considers economically or politically important,” Meyers said. The active campaign attributed to Vapor Panda is separate from the ARTEX activity Microsoft Threat Intelligence attributed to Storm-0940 earlier this month, including a supply-chain attack targeting ConnectWise customers.  Adversarial use of AI is relatively new, yet also quickly becoming the new normal, Meyers said. “We’re scrambling because we’re seeing so many of these agentic adversaries.” Agentic AI use for malicious purposes is growing month-over-month at a rate of almost threefold. CrowdStrike observed roughly 45 agentic adversary attacks in September and it’s already at 126 for October, and climbing. Adversarial use of agentic AI isn’t an intractable problem, but rather another reminder that organizations need visibility into their endpoints, identities and cross-domain capabilities, Meyers said.  These attacks aren’t showcasing anything new, “it’s just doing it at a speed and scale that we’re unaccustomed to,” he said. “It’s not hopeless, but you’ve got to take action. You can’t put your head in the sand.” The post China-backed threat group used agentic AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets in 11 days appeared first on CyberScoop .

title: Stealthy GJ-21 Drone Has Launched And Recovered From Type 076 Amphibious Assault Ship, China Claims
zh_title: 中国声称GJ-21隐形无人机已从076型两栖攻击舰发射并回收
summary: 据中国人民解放军称，一架GJ-21隐形飞翼无人作战飞机（UCAV）已在076型两栖攻击舰四川舰上成功发射并回收。这一里程碑的目视确认尚未出现，但有稳定的迹象表明，配备电磁弹射器的四川号正在准备飞行试验。 GJ-21 已经被发现从陆地机场起飞。此前网上出现的一张 GJ-21 无人机的图片。中国互联网 GJ-21和陆基GJ-11神秘龙它是
content:
据中国人民解放军称，一架GJ-21隐形飞翼无人作战飞机（UCAV）已在076型两栖攻击舰四川舰上成功发射并回收。这一里程碑的目视确认尚未出现，但有稳定的迹象表明，配备电磁弹射器的四川号正在准备飞行试验。 GJ-21 已经被发现从陆地机场起飞。此前网上出现的一张 GJ-21 无人机的图片。中国互联网 GJ-21 及其所基于的陆基 GJ-11 神秘龙是中国在无人战斗机和其他飞翼型无人机方面进行重大投资的典型例子。这些进展与美国军方至少在公开场合回避此类设计形成鲜明对比。尽管美国过去在这一领域取得了重大成就，包括开发舰载无人战斗机，但情况仍然如此。解放军海军现在看来有望成为第一个拥有此类作战能力的国家。 076型两栖攻击舰四川舰的库存图片。解放军“中国首架舰载隐形侦察攻击无人机‘GJ-21’最近在 076 型两栖攻击舰‘四川’号（舷号 51）上首次成功起降，”解放军官方喉舌“X”上的“中国军号”账户今天发布的一篇文章称。
“这是中国两栖攻击舰发展的又一重大突破，表明中国海军现已具备在大型海上作战平台上操作固定翼隐形无人机的能力。”截至撰写本文时，解放军和中国官方媒体都没有透露这些试验发生的地点或时间，也没有提供任何其他详细信息，包括总共进行了多少次发射和回收。到目前为止，尚未发布试验的官方图片或视频。中国军号在 X 上发布的关于 GJ-21 和 076 型的帖子中附有一张图片。解放军/中国军号未经证实的说法称 GJ-21 是从四川发射的，本月早些时候已经开始在社交媒体上流传。顺便说一句，通过前起落架支柱上的弹射杆，可以很容易地将 GJ-21 与陆基 GJ-11 区分开来。两条有趣的 076 型新闻： 2. 通过 Temstar/SDF：“洋基在今晚的 Chahuahui 节目中确认 076 已经发射了 GJ-21。他也以非常直接的方式说道，基本上“你们可以停止猜测，我可以直接告诉你们：是的，他们发射了 GJ-21”。” pic.twitter.com/ODkl6Kki9A — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) 2026 年 10 月 15 日 对 Planet Labs 卫星图像的审查确实显示，截至 10 月 13 日，四川号仍在上海沪东中华的常规泊位，但四天后就消失了。目前尚不清楚它何时离开港口。
这艘独一无二的 076 型似乎直到 10 月 26 日才返回。TWZ 还获得了今天从 Vantor 拍摄的沪东中华号卫星图像，可以看到这艘船仍然停泊在码头上，如本文顶部和下面所示。 GJ-21 无人机，或更可能是其模型，也已经出现在码头上一段时间了。 2026 年 10 月 10 日，位于沪东中华造船厂的 076 型两栖攻击舰四川号。右图还可以看到被广泛评估为大型无人水下航行器 (UUV) 母舰的船只。卫星图像 ©2026 Vantor

【原文 English Original】
A GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) has successfully launched from and recovered aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan , according to China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA). Visual confirmation of this milestone has yet to emerge, but there have been steady signs of preparations for flight trials from the Sichuan , which features an electromagnetic catapult. GJ-21s have already been spotted flying from airfields on land. A picture of a GJ-21 drone that previously emerged online. Chinese internet The GJ-21 and the land-based GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon it is based on are prime examples of China’s major investments in UCAVs and other flying-wing-type drones. These developments stand in particular contrast to the U.S. military’s eschewing of such designs , at least publicly . This is despite significant past U.S. achievements in this arena, including in the development of carrier-based UCAVs. The PLA Navy (PLAN) now looks to be on track to be the first country to field an operational capability of this kind. A stock picture of the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . PLA “China’s first ship-borne stealth reconnaissance and attack drone ‘GJ-21’ recently made its first successful take-off and landing on [the Type] 076 amphibious assault ship, the ‘Sichuan’ (Hull 51),” according to a post today from the China Military Bugle account on X, an official PLA mouthpiece. “This is another significant breakthrough in the development of China’s amphibious assault ship, indicating that the Chinese Navy now has the capability to operate fixed-wing stealth drones from large maritime combat platforms.” At the time of writing, neither the PLA nor Chinese state media have shared where or when these trials occurred or provided any other additional details, including how many total launches and recoveries were conducted. No official pictures or videos from the testing have been released so far. A graphic that accompanied the post on the China Military Bugle’s account on X regarding the GJ-21 and the Type 076. PLA/China Military Bugle Unconfirmed claims that a GJ-21 had been launched from Sichuan had already begun circulating on social media earlier this month. As an aside, the GJ-21 is readily discernible from the land-based GJ-11 by the catapult bar on its nose landing gear strut. Two interesting Type 076 News: 2. Via Temstar/SDF: "Yankee confirmed on tonight's Chahuahui that 076 has launched a GJ-21. He said it in a very straight forward way too, basically "you guys can stop guessing, I can tell you straight: yes they launched a GJ-21"." pic.twitter.com/ODkl6Kki9A — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) October 15, 2026 A review of satellite imagery from Planet Labs does show Sichuan was at its usual berth at Hudong-Zhonghua in Shanghai as of October 13, but absent four days later. When exactly it left port is unclear. The one-of-a-kind Type 076 does not appear to have returned until October 26. TWZ has also obtained a satellite image of Hudong-Zhonghua taken just today from Vantor, with the ship still seen sitting at the pier, as seen at the top of this story and below. GJ-21 drones, or more likely mockups thereof, have also been present on the pier for some time. The Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan at the Hudong-Zhonghua shipyard on October 10, 2026. What is widely assessed to be a mothership for large uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUV) is also seen at right. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor Even while Sichuan was still under construction, there were growing signs that a navalized version of the GJ-11, as well as other uncrewed platforms, would be major components of its future air wing . With its electromagnetic catapult and notably large overall size, the Type 076 is unlike any other big-deck amphibious warship in service today globally, as TWZ has previously explored in depth . A pair of apparent GJ-11 mockups at a test and/or training site on Changxing Island in Shanghai in May 2024, near where the Type 076 was under construction at the time. Google Earth As mentioned, there have been further signs that the PLA has been preparing Sichuan for real launches and recoveries, especially of GJ-21s, since last year. Pictures emerged online in October 2025 showing a red-colored test ‘truck’ on the ship’s flight deck, indicating the start of catapult testing. Video from those tests has since been released. Weighted trucks like this have long been used to test catapults on aircraft carriers during construction  or following maintenance . The Type 076 left port for the first time in November 2025. 小紅車上線了 pic.twitter.com/zrptPDwu2X — 飞刀 (@chaoyinsukandao) October 28, 2025 Weighted carts catapult test on Type 076 LHD three lines marked directly under and outside the wheels of the Red cart to ensure it is centered the parallel alignment markings flanking the catapult slot serve as visual tips for precise positioning https://t.co/KJkC2ZrLgS pic.twitter.com/pZa0Vx56jG — David Wang (@DavidWangPLA) August 1, 2026 “Two GJ-21 aircraft were displayed at the victory parade in September 2025, reportedly having entered PLAN service in mid-2025,” according to Andreas Rupprecht , an expert on Chinese aviation and contributor to TWZ . “By late 2025, several GJ-21 aircraft were reportedly undergoing simulated EMALS launches and arrested landings at the PLAN’s land-based facility at Huangdicun .” In February of this year, GJ-21 mockups were spotted on Sichuan ’s flight deck and riding on the ship’s port-side elevator to the hangar deck as part of what appeared to be deck-handling trials. After the first Type 076 LHD/LAH "Sichuan" was seen yesterday with a GJ-21 UCAV mock-up on deck, the GJ-21 was seen for the first time with its wings folded and later lowered to the hangar deck on one of the elevators. (Images @鼎盛大彪 from Weibo) pic.twitter.com/eMyz2QLHQX — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) February 1, 2026 More recent satellite imagery had shown that the Type 076’s flight deck had received additional markings in line with progress toward real flight operations. Fittings for three arresting cables also became plainly visible. Those cables are also notably depicted in the graphic that the China Military Bugle shared online today. The arresting gear fittings as seen in the October 30, 2026, satellite image from Vantor, at left, as well as how they are depicted in the graphic from the China Military Bugle. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/PLA The GJ-21 will of course not be the only aircraft in the Type 076’s future air wing. The ship is also expected to carry a variety of other uncrewed aircraft, as well as crewed helicopters. China has shown a range of other combat drone designs in recent years. Navalized versions could well be developed for deployment on Sichuan , as well as PLAN’s growing fleet of traditional carriers and other suitable configured vessels. Loading the Type 076 with operational UCAVs would only underscore the significance of this particular ship. As we have previously written : “The potential value to the PLAN of having a fleet of very large deck amphibious assault ships that are highly capable of large-scale drone operations as well as traditional amphibious assaults is clear. These ships could be used to launch and recover UCAVs like the GJ-11 and other types of drones to perform a host of missions from maritime strike to intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). They could be used to provide additional ‘mass’ in support of the operations of larger carrier strike groups and help to free the air wings of flattops like Fujian up for tasks they might be better suited for. In addition, they could provide a lower tier of naval aviation support that could be employed independently.” … “Simply having more naval aviation capacity overall would give the PLAN added flexibility for various operations closer to the mainland, including a potential military intervention against Taiwan or defending its expansive and largely unrecognized territorial claims in places like the South China Sea . Type 076s could also help project naval and air power further from China’s shores, something that has also been a driving factor behind the country’s broader carrier ambitions .” … “The Type 076 could help provide support during humanitarian assistance and disaster relief operations. Big deck amphibious warfare ships, in general, provide their operators with immensely valuable platforms for projecting both hard and soft power .” Last year, the PLA separately confirmed that the GJ-11 had entered at least limited operational service. That followed a steady ramp-up in testing of that drone based on what could be seen in satellite imagery and video clips that had emerged online. This included evidence of near-daily flights at Malan Air Base, a  major hub for testing uncrewed platforms . GJ-11s had also been spotted at an operational air base in China’s Tibet Autonomous Region. New video out from the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China shows the new GJ-11 stealth drone (UCAV), and also the J-20 stealth fighter firing a live PL-15 air-to-air missile: pic.twitter.com/wraDqyMOht — The STRATCOM Bureau (@OSPSF) November 11, 2025 As mentioned earlier, the continued development of the GJ-11 and GJ-21 are reflective of the PLA’s broader pursuit of stealthy flying-wing drones, which is not limited to UCAVs. Several larger designs that look most immediately suited to high-altitude, long-endurance ISR missions have also broken cover in the country in the past few years. There is something of a trend in this regard globally, with Russia , India , Turkey , and France also pursuing flying-wing drone designs. The U.S. military continues to be markedly absent from this space, at least that we know , despite major investments and real demonstrations of relevant capability, before various programs were abandoned for reasons that still remain largely unclear . In the late 2010s, the U.S. Navy notably looked to be right on the edge of fielding a carrier-based UCAV, before changing course entirely to an uncrewed tanker instead. There are some signs now that the service may be taking another look at the capabilities it passed over. It is still to be seen how quickly the PLA’s official statement today will be followed by real confirmation of the launching and recovery of a GJ-21 from the Sichuan . Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post Stealthy GJ-21 Drone Has Launched And Recovered From Type 076 Amphibious Assault Ship, China Claims appeared first on TWZ .

zh_title: 澳大利亚国防部长称中国军力建设给东南亚造成“压力”
summary: 澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯周四表示，中国的军力建设正在东南亚制造“压力状况”，并敦促盟友和伙伴深化合作。菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗于 2026 年 10 月 29 日在宿务举行的第 13 届东盟国防部长扩大会议 (ADMM-Plus) 上致开幕词。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。北京部署了数百艘海岸警卫队、海军和其他船只在南海有争议的地区巡逻，尽管国际裁决认为其立场毫无根据，但中国对南海几乎完全拥有主权
content:
澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯周四表示，中国的军力建设正在东南亚制造“压力状况”，并敦促盟友和伙伴深化合作。菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗于 2026 年 10 月 29 日在宿务举行的第 13 届东盟国防部长扩大会议 (ADMM-Plus) 上致开幕词。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。北京部署了数百艘海岸警卫队、海军和其他船只在南海有争议的地区巡逻，尽管国际裁决认为其立场没有法律依据，但中国对南海几乎全部海域拥有主权。 7月，澳大利亚抗议中国在南太平洋试射核导弹，称此次发射“破坏稳定”。马尔斯周四在菲律宾举行的东南亚国防部长会议间隙对记者表示：“我们显然看到了自第二次世界大战结束以来世界上最大规模的常规军事集结。” “中国没有解释为什么要这样做，所有这些都在创造压力的条件。”他补充说，北京日益增强的自信给堪培拉“带来了挑战”，并表示澳大利亚依赖于维持现有的基于规则的秩序。 “我们需要确保我们对道路规则的理解继续适用，因为对于像澳大利亚这样的中等强国来说，实际上是规则赋予了我们代理权，”他说。
澳大利亚国防部长理查德·马勒斯 (Richard Marles) 于 2026 年 10 月 29 日抵达宿雾举行的第 13 届东盟国防部长扩大会议 (ADMM-Plus)。照片：Ezra Acayan/法新社。中国在南海人工岛日益增强的自信和军事化促使堪培拉和华盛顿深化与一些东南亚国家的防务合作。 “小队”马勒斯周四表示，他会见了“小队”，这是一个由澳大利亚、日本、美国和菲律宾组成的非正式国防和安全组织，他们承诺加强国防政策协调。他说：“我认为所有四个国家都充分理解世界这一地区面临的挑战和所经历的压力。”他补充说：“现在是时候加倍努力帮助朋友和邻国，并更加密切地合作以保障我们的集体安全。”另请参阅：中国“热爱和平”，但可以“轻松赢得”与菲律宾的对抗——大使 菲律宾是澳大利亚的亲密安全伙伴，多年来一直在南海与中国对抗。马尼拉本月早些时候表示，9月份，中国在关键水道有争议地区的军事和海岸警卫队数量几乎增加了一倍。

【原文 English Original】
Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said Thursday that China’s military build-up was creating a “condition of pressure” in Southeast Asia, and urged allies and partners to deepen cooperation. Philippines Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro delivers his opening remarks during the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu on October 29, 2026. Photo: Eloisa Lopez/AFP. Beijing deploys hundreds of coast guard, navy and other vessels to patrol disputed areas of the South China Sea, which it claims almost entirely despite an international ruling that its position has no legal basis. In July, Australia protested China’s test of a nuclear-capable missile in the South Pacific, calling the launch “destabilising”. “We’re obviously seeing the biggest conventional military build-up that the world has seen since the end of the Second World War from China,” Marles told reporters Thursday on the sidelines of a meeting of Southeast Asian defence ministers in the Philippines. “There’s not an explanation from China as to why it’s doing this, and all of that is creating the condition of pressure.” Beijing’s growing assertiveness was “providing challenges” for Canberra, he added, saying Australia relied on maintaining the existing rules-based order. “We need to be ensuring that how we understand the rules of the road continue to apply, because for a middle power like Australia, it is actually the rules which give us agency,” he said. Australia’s Defence Minister Richard Marles arrives before the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu on October 29, 2026. Photo: Ezra Acayan/AFP. China’s growing assertiveness and militarisation of artificial islands in the South China Sea have spurred Canberra, as well as Washington, to deepen defence cooperation with some Southeast Asian countries. The ‘Squad’ Marles said Thursday that he met with the “Squad”, an informal defence and security group composed of Australia, Japan, the United States and the Philippines, where they committed to greater defence policy coordination. “I think the challenges that are being faced in this part of the world and the pressures that are being experienced are well understood by all four countries,” he said. “Now is a time to double down on friends and to double down on neighbours and to be working more closely together to provide for our collective security,” he added. See also: China ‘loves peace’ but could ‘easily win’ confrontation with Philippines – ambassador The Philippines, a close security partner of Australia, has been engaged in years of confrontations with China in the South China Sea. China’s military and coast guard presence in contested areas of the critical waterway nearly doubled in September, Manila said earlier this month.
