content:
中国A股连续遭重挫后，央行星期一（11月2日）宣布，将推动证券、基金、保险公司互换便利操作，以及将股票回购增持再贷款政策转为长期制度性安排。 （路透社）
中国A股上月连续遭重挫后，央行宣布开展证券、基金、保险公司互换便利操作，股票回购增持再贷款政策则转为长期制度性安排，以支持资本市场健康稳定发展。上证指数星期一（11月2日）上涨1.1%，创下8月27日以来最大单日涨幅。
分析指出，上述政策主要是为加大流动性、托底稳预期，但不太可能复制2024年首次使用上述政策工具后的反弹行情。
中国央行和金融监管总局、中国证监会等部门星期一召开座谈会，研究部署用好用足政策工具的有关工作。央行同日闭市后作出上述宣布。
其中，互换便利操作将于星期二（3日）展开。目前有31家证券、基金公司申报，申请额度超过1000亿元（人民币，约192亿新元）。此外，股票回购增持再贷款政策由阶段性安排转为长期制度性安排，再贷款利率由1.25%降至1%。
中金公司、国泰海通证券、中信证券以及工商银行、建设银行、中信银行等23家证券和基金公司以及26家银行参加了会议。
中国金融监管机构2024年9月首次推出互换便利操作和股票回购增持再贷款两项政策工具，前者通过向证券、基金和保险机构提供流动性，增强入市投资能力；后者则通过低成本贷款，鼓励上市公司回购股票及主要股东增持股份。政策当时推出后，股市随即迎来强劲反弹。
今年6月以来，A股进入震荡期。A股基准指数沪深300指数上月下跌8.5%，创2016年以来最大单月跌幅；上证指数则在10月最后一个交易日收报3599点，时隔一年多再次失守3600点关口；创业板指10月份累计重挫23.02%，创2016年2月以来最大单月跌幅。
股市低迷、信心受挫之际，央行第三次推出上述两项政策工具。中国证监会指出，此次推出的工具扩大了互换便利业务的参与机构范围和资金额度；同时提高上市公司股票回购增持专项再贷款的覆盖率；证监会将引导推出更多权重指数公司、龙头科技股等具有较强市场影响的标志性案例。
受政策预期带动，沪深300指数当日收高0.8%，科创50指数收盘涨幅超过3%。
华侨银行亚洲宏观经济主管谢栋铭告诉《联合早报》，这次重点是降低使用门槛和成本，把已有额度真正用起来，解决现有资本市场支持工具“有额度、但使用不足；有资金、但传导不畅”的问题。
他同时指出，央行可以改善金融机构融资能力，但无法直接消除机构对股票市场下跌的担忧。“机构是否愿意增加股票配置，仍取决于融资成本、预期投资回报、市场波动及自身风险管理要求。”
谢栋铭和香颂资本执行董事沈萌均认为，此轮政策支持不太可能复制2024年的强反弹行情。沈萌认为，相关政策工具可能会达到预期管理和稳定市场情绪的目的，但对股市总体来说是“治标不治本”。
他解释：“如果只是支持资本市场，而没有改善实体经济基本面，就会让市场跟基本面脱节。这也会鼓励更多人短线投机操作，导致整个资本市场基础更加脆弱，陷入恶性循环。”
银河证券原首席经济学家左小蕾也说，中国股市容易受非理性情绪驱动，靠注入资金或许会有短期效应，但更需要长期的资本市场建设，包括提高上市公司的质量和业绩等。“如果没有这种公司给市场提供信心，股民就更容易选择短期套利的方式炒股。”

content:
Digital Agency 提供人工智能应用程序来帮助起草议会答案 - 日本时报
Digital Agency 提供人工智能应用程序来帮助起草议会答案
数字机构启动了一款人工智能应用程序的试用，以帮助政府官员起草立法者问题的答案，并在议会会议前了解他们的意图。 |约翰·布鲁克斯
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
Digital Agency 已开始试用一款应用程序，利用其 Gennai 生成人工智能平台帮助起草议员在议会提出的问题的答案，该平台可供约 18 万名政府工作人员使用。
该应用程序还可以帮助政府官员提前更好地了解立法者问题背后的意图。
该机构计划在本届国会或日本议会会议期间评估该应用程序的有效性，目标是从明年的国会例行会议开始全面运营。
当立法者的问题输入应用程序时，人工智能会组织和分析其要点，并根据过去的政府答案和国会审议记录在几分钟内生成多个答案草案。
该应用程序包括根据不同目的调整写作风格的功能，例如明确政策方向的“政策解释”模式和反映政治考量的“政治判断”模式。
政府官员可以直接编辑答案草稿。该应用程序还可以预测立法者提出的后续问题。该机构强调，官员们将继续负责澄清政策决定、整理政府观点并最终确定答案，并强调决策不会交给人工智能。
数字化转型大臣古川敏晴在周五的新闻发布会上表示：“我们可以提高工作效率，并找到有助于国会更深入审议的答案，这非常好。” “我还想听听其他部长的反馈。”

Digital Agency offers AI app to help draft parliamentary answers - The Japan Times
Digital Agency offers AI app to help draft parliamentary answers
The Digital Agency has launched a trial of an artificial intelligence-powered app to help government officials draft answers to lawmakers’ questions and understand their intent ahead of parliamentary sessions. | JOHAN BROOKS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
The Digital Agency has started offering, on a trial basis, an app that helps draft answers to lawmakers’ questions in parliament, using its Gennai generative artificial intelligence platform, which is available to about 180,000 government workers.
The app also helps government officials better understand the intent behind lawmakers’ questions in advance.
The agency plans to evaluate the app’s effectiveness during the current session of the Diet, or Japan’s parliament, with the aim to put it into full-scale operation from next year’s ordinary Diet session.
When a lawmaker’s question is entered into the app, AI organizes and analyzes its key points and generates multiple draft answers within minutes based on past government answers and minutes of Diet deliberations.
The app includes a function that adjusts writing styles for different purposes, such as a “policy explanation” mode to clarify policy direction and a “political judgment” mode to reflect political considerations.
Government officials can edit the draft answers directly. The app can also predict follow-up questions from lawmakers. The agency emphasized that officials will remain responsible for clarifying policy decisions, organizing the government’s views and finalizing answers, stressing that decision-making will not be left to AI.
“It’s very good that we can improve our work efficiency and create answers that contribute to deeper Diet deliberations,” digital transformation minister Toshiharu Furukawa told a news conference Friday. “I’d also like to hear feedback from other ministers.”

The coalition that emerges in Johannesburg will influence negotiations in councils across South Africa. Six polls offer different scenarios for the City.
Illustrative image: DA Joburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille. (Photo: Per-Anders Pettersson / Getty Images) | EFF Joburg mayoral candidate Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng. (Photo: Supplied / Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng) | ActionSA mayoral candidate Herman Mashaba. (Photo: Bheki Simelane) |
Johannesburg is the fulcrum that could balance – or topple – the house of cards that is coalition politics in local government. Make no mistake, the coalition that will emerge in Johannesburg will not be independent of the ones in Tshwane, Nelson Mandela Bay, Mogale City or Rustenburg.
The ANC has confirmed that coalition negotiations will be run from the office of party Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula, while the DA’s federal executive has the final say on any coalition agreements involving the party.
If the Johannesburg council can assemble a stable coalition over the next few weeks, the hope of stability will rise across the other metros. The threats of provincial administration from Premier Panyaza Lesufi and of withholding grants from Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana will recede as well.
What happens after the vote? Councils, coalitions and (maybe) controversies
What are the chances of a stable coalition being formed in Johannesburg? If the six Johannesburg polls conducted over the last four months are any indication, the chances are fair to slim without a change in the attitude of political parties big and small – unless a grand coalition of the ANC and the DA clears the board.
The bar charts below summarise the results of six polls held between mid-June and mid-October. There have been two polls from Ipsos, two from The Common Sense/Social Research Foundation, and one each from News24/Sabi and eNCA/Markdata.
Before reviewing the numbers, it’s important to remember that the four pollsters used different survey sizes and methodologies, including the questions around voter preferences. We will come back to this soon.
The DA came first in every poll except for the first Ipsos poll. In three of the polls (both The Common Sense/Social Research Foundation polls and the eNCA/Markdata poll), the DA had at least 35% of respondents’ support, and the gap between the DA and the ANC was at least 13 percentage points.
The DA polled at only 29.2% in the News24/Sabi poll, but when the poll allocated the 14% of respondents who identified as non-DA voters but who said there was a “fair chance” of them voting for the DA, the party’s vote rose to 39.6%, and the ANC’s fell to 19.7%.
These numbers are not very different from The Common Sense/Social Research Foundation’s first poll, by far the most favourable for the DA. There are two lessons here: first, how you ask a question matters if you want to understand voting intent, and second, the squeezing of opposition parties could be the difference between a DA in government and one that remains in opposition.
There are five large parties in Johannesburg: the DA, ANC, MK, EFF and ActionSA. The polls have them winning between 84% and 91% of the vote. Only the DA or the ANC can head a coalition.
The DA refuses to work with the EFF and MK; the party is also not fond of the PA. That leaves the ANC or ActionSA as coalition partners.
If the DA does as well on Wednesday as in the first Common Sense poll, the party should have no problem forming a coalition with either party. The chart below shows how a DA-ActionSA coalition could achieve a majority.
If the election results are closer to the numbers in the eNCA/Markdata poll, the DA’s job of forming a coalition without the ANC falls pretty much to zero. The chart below shows that a DA-ActionSA coalition would need the seats of every small party just to make it halfway.
Of course, if the results look anything like either of the Ipsos polls, then the DA has no path to government without the ANC – and any coalition between the top two parties would be on more equal terms than previous scenarios.
The ANC is the party with a full range of options for coalition partners under the latest Ipsos polling conditions. With ActionSA, an ANC-EFF coalition would need just one more seat for a majority.
For the DA, any share of the vote above 40% should put it in a commanding position to form a coalition. Anything below 35% and the party would prefer to remain in opposition unless it can form a coalition with the ANC as the senior partner. Any share of the vote within this range could still mean victory for the DA, if it has the appetite for another round of coalition politics. DM

content:

台湾男子因涉嫌诈骗和非法拘留在马尼拉被捕
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。

中新社马尼拉11月2日电 菲律宾警方称，一名台湾男子因涉嫌非法拘禁菲律宾公民并强迫他们进行网络恋爱和电信诈骗而在菲律宾首都被捕。
菲律宾国家警察刑事调查和侦查组（CIDG）表示，在收到一名妇女伴侣的投诉后，警方于10月28日突击搜查了马尼拉马拉特区的一个公寓单元，称她遭到非法限制和虐待。
此次行动营救了三名菲律宾受害者（两名女性和一名男性），并逮捕了一名 32 岁的彭姓台湾男子和一名 38 岁的马来西亚李姓男子。
据刑事调查小组称，两名嫌疑人面临人口贩运、非法拘留和胁迫等指控。
初步调查发现，嫌疑人招募菲律宾国民担任所谓的“虚拟助理”职位，提供月薪400美元至500美元，外加100美元的全勤奖金。
然而，在接受工作后，三名受害者据称从 10 月 23 日起被限制在公寓内，手机被没收。据报道，他们被迫从上午 9 点工作到晚上 9 点。每天，背诵爱情和电信诈骗的剧本。
警方表示，受害者在被转移到菲律宾中部的保和岛之前已获救。
CIDG 表示，警方在突袭中查获了笔记本电脑、手机、身份证和含有可疑诈骗脚本的文件。
据台湾刑侦局驻菲律宾联络官透露，彭来自南投县，有多次诈骗前科，经常前往菲律宾和柬埔寨。
台北驻菲律宾经济文化办事处周一表示，将于周二在万灵节假期后政府办公室重新开放后派人员探访彭，以核实他的身份并监督调查。

Taiwanese man arrested in Manila over alleged scam, illegal detention
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Image from Pixabay for illustrative purpose only
Manila, Nov. 2 (CNA) A Taiwanese man has been arrested in the Philippine capital on suspicion of unlawfully detaining Filipino nationals and forcing them to carry out online romance and telecom scams, Philippine police said.
The Philippine National Police Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) said officers raided a condominium unit in Manila's Malate district on Oct. 28 after receiving a complaint from a woman's partner that she had been unlawfully confined and abused.
The operation led to the rescue of three Filipino victims -- two women and one man -- and the arrest of a 32-year-old Taiwanese man surnamed Peng (彭) and a 38-year-old Malaysian man surnamed Lee.
The two suspects face charges including human trafficking, illegal detention and coercion, according to the CIDG.
A preliminary investigation found that the suspects recruited Filipino nationals for purported "virtual assistant" positions, offering monthly salaries of US$400-US$500 plus a US$100 attendance bonus.
However, after accepting the jobs, the three victims were allegedly confined in the condominium from Oct. 23, with their mobile phones confiscated. They were reportedly forced to work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. each day, memorizing scripts for romance and telecom scams.
Police said the victims were rescued before they could be transferred to Bohol in the central Philippines.
Officers seized laptops, mobile phones, identification cards and documents containing suspected scam scripts during the raid, the CIDG said.
According to Taiwan's Criminal Investigation Bureau liaison officer in the Philippines, Peng is from Nantou County, has multiple prior fraud convictions and frequently traveled to the Philippines and Cambodia.
The Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in the Philippines said Monday it will send personnel to visit Peng on Tuesday, after government offices reopen following the All Souls' Day holiday, to verify his identity and monitor the investigation.

content:
广泛的行业联盟敦促永久暂停对与中国相关的船舶征收昂贵的美国港口费用
广泛的行业联盟敦促永久暂停对与中国相关的船舶征收昂贵的美国港口费用
由海事、农业、制造、零售和物流组织组成的广泛联盟正在敦促特朗普政府永久暂停针对与中国有关的船只征收美国港口费用，并警告称，恢复收费将增加美国企业的成本，损害出口商并扰乱全球供应链。
在 10 月 30 日致美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔 (Jamieson Greer) 的信中，该联盟欢迎将 301 条款船舶收费暂停期限延长两个月至 2027 年 1 月 9 日的提议，但呼吁华盛顿采取进一步行动，永久取消这些费用。
签署方包括美国商会、全国制造商协会、全国零售联合会、美国农业局联合会、美国港务局协会、国际航运商会和世界航运理事会，以及代表依赖海洋运输的企业的数百个其他贸易协会。
这些组织认为，恢复收费将给已经在运费上涨、设备可用性挑战和全球贸易不确定性中苦苦挣扎的供应链增加另一层成本。
由于中国制造的船舶在全球航运能力中占据很大份额，该联盟警告说，影响将远远超出中国航运公司的范围，影响美国进出口商的船舶部署和运输成本。
这封信还引发了人们对针对外国建造的滚装船的规定的担忧，这可能会影响美国盟国的航运公司，并扰乱美国制造商所依赖的运输服务。
对于进口商来说，这些费用可能意味着更高的运输附加费以及消费品和工业投入品的价格上涨。对于包括农产品生产商和制造商在内的出口商来说，这些收费可能会降低美国产品在海外市场的竞争力。
该联盟还质疑港口收费将有意义地重建美国陷入困境的商业造船业的想法。
这些组织认为，中国主导地位背后的根本挑战，包括美国造船能力有限、劳动力短缺和缺乏竞争性替代品等，仍未得到解决。
相反，他们呼吁制定专门的长期造船战略，并得到公共和私营部门持续投资和承诺的支持。
世界航运理事会单独向美国贸易代表办公室提交了意见，支持振兴美国造船业的努力，但认为持续的立法措施、政府支持和劳动力发展将比大幅征收船舶费用更有效。
最新的行业呼吁是在特朗普政府于 10 月 23 日提议将暂停期限延长至 2027 年 1 月 9 日之后发出的，华盛顿和北京正在继续就中国在海事、物流和造船领域的主导地位进行谈判。
这些费用最初于 2025 年 10 月征收，随后根据更广泛的中美贸易协议于次月暂停征收。除非提议的延期生效，否则现有的暂停计划将于 11 月 9 日到期。
推动永久暂停的努力是在立法者和海事部门相互竞争的压力下进行的。

Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
A broad coalition of maritime, agricultural, manufacturing, retail and logistics organizations is urging the Trump administration to permanently suspend U.S. port fees targeting China-linked vessels, warning that reinstating the charges would raise costs for American businesses, hurt exporters and disrupt global supply chains.
In an October 30 letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, the coalition welcomed the proposed two-month extension of the Section 301 vessel fee suspension through January 9, 2027, but called on Washington to go further and eliminate the charges permanently.
Signatories include the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, National Association of Manufacturers, National Retail Federation, American Farm Bureau Federation, American Association of Port Authorities, International Chamber of Shipping and World Shipping Council, along with hundreds of other trade associations representing businesses that depend on ocean transportation.
The groups argue that reinstating the fees would add another layer of costs to supply chains already struggling with elevated freight rates, equipment availability challenges and uncertainty in global trade.
Because Chinese-built ships account for a significant share of global shipping capacity, the coalition warned that the impact would extend well beyond Chinese shipping companies, affecting vessel deployments and transportation costs for American importers and exporters.
The letter also raised concerns about provisions targeting foreign-built roll-on/roll-off vessels, which could affect shipping companies from U.S. allied nations and disrupt transportation services relied upon by American manufacturers.
For importers, the fees could mean higher transportation surcharges and increased prices for consumer goods and industrial inputs. For exporters, including agricultural producers and manufacturers, the charges could make American products less competitive in overseas markets.
The coalition also challenged the idea that port fees would meaningfully rebuild America’s struggling commercial shipbuilding industry.
The groups argued that the underlying challenges behind China’s dominance, including limited U.S. shipbuilding capacity, workforce shortages and a lack of competitive alternatives, remain unresolved.
Instead, they called for a dedicated long-term shipbuilding strategy backed by sustained investment and commitments from both the public and private sectors.
The World Shipping Council separately submitted comments to USTR, supporting efforts to revitalize American shipbuilding but arguing that sustained legislative measures, government support and workforce development would be more effective than sweeping vessel fees.
The latest industry appeal follows the Trump administration’s October 23 proposal to extend the suspension through January 9, 2027, as Washington and Beijing continue negotiations over China’s dominance of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors.
The fees were originally imposed in October 2025 before being suspended the following month under a broader U.S.-China trade agreement. The existing suspension is scheduled to expire November 9 unless the proposed extension takes effect.
The push for a permanent suspension comes amid competing pressure from lawmakers and maritime labor unions, which argue that the fees are necessary to counter China’s state-supported shipbuilding industry and encourage investment in American shipyards.
Senators Mark Kelly and Elizabeth Warren have previously urged the administration to reinstate the charges, warning that the suspension undermines efforts to rebuild U.S. commercial shipbuilding capacity.

content:
资料照片：美国伊利诺伊州的玉米收成。(2015年9月23日)
今年5月美中两国达成协议，中国同意未来三年每年购买170亿美元的美国农产品，但数据显示，今年以来，中国对美国大豆以外的农产品购买量降到七年来的最低水平，中国是否能落实协议承诺引发关注。
路透社星期一(11月2日)报道，虽然美中两国在今年5月唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统访问中国时，达成了中国从2026年起至2028年每年向美国采购170亿美元的美国农产品。
但根据海关数据显示，从今年1月到9月，中国仅购买了价值72亿美元从肉类到玉米的非大豆农产品，这一购买量是自2019年美中首次贸易战以来的最低。
今年5月特朗普总统在北京与中国国家主席习近平会晤后，美国白宫在公布的事实简报中说，美中达成的贸易成果之一是中国承诺于2026年至2028年每年向美国购买170亿美元的农产品。其中2026年的采购额将按比例计算。
白宫当时表示，170亿美元不包括中国在2025年10月已经作出的美国大豆采购承诺。此前，美中在2025年多轮相互加征关税后，双边农产品贸易大幅萎缩。
不过，中国官方当时的公开声明没有提到170亿美元这一具体数字。中国商务部仅表示，美中双方在经贸磋商中取得“积极的成果”，将继续解决非关税壁垒以及部分农产品市场准入问题。
路透社星期一报道，目前尚不清楚北京是否违反了协议承诺，因为白宫没有说明2026年的按比例计算是从5月宣布后就开始，还是要等中国拟议中的关税下调最终落实后才开始，而关税安排目前尚未敲定。不过中国缓慢的采购进度给170亿美元承诺能否按期完成增加了许多不确定性。
今年9月，在特朗普总统结束与中国国家主席习近平在华盛顿的会晤后，美国白宫发布的情况说明指出，美中两国就相互给予300亿美元非敏感商品更优惠关税待遇的建议达成了共识。美方享受关税优惠的出口商品包括农产品、鱼类及海鲜、原木与木制品、化妆品以及医疗器械。此外，美中贸易委员会还成立了一个工作组，致力于解决农业领域的市场准入壁垒问题。
然而，路透社报道指出，中国缓慢的采购进度让美国农民担心中国可能无法履行承诺，加上高燃料价格，这一问题可能对美国中期选举带来影响。
报道援引美国高粱生产者协会首席执行官蒂姆·拉斯特(Tim Lust)的话说：“我们的种植者都是爱国者，但仓库里存放满满的谷物，我们也希望看到谷物的采购。”他表示，大豆采购交易确实在进行，但没有看到其他农产品的交易。
上个月，中国国有贸易商购买了8至10船美国大豆，总量估计为52万至65万吨，是9月份特习峰会后，中方进行的首批大规模美国大豆采购。
路透社报道，2021年，美国向中国出口的高粱达到高峰，达到650万吨，价值21亿美元，现在则面临来自巴西的竞争。2025年9月巴西获得了进入中国市场的许可，今年到目前为止，巴西已向中国出口了170万吨高粱，还计划再运近100万吨。
美国之音就中国的农产品采购问题向白宫和美国贸易代表办公室发出置评请求，至报道发表前还未收到回应。

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

孟加拉国达卡，服装工人封锁道路，要求提高最低工资，警察发射催泪弹。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 3 日 01:05
更新于 2026 年 11 月 3 日 01:16
达卡 - 孟加拉国的服装工厂在前一天大范围停工后于 11 月 2 日短暂恢复运营，但工人和警察之间的新冲突迫使数百家工厂再次暂停生产。
骚乱引发了人们对孟加拉国发货延误和买家信心的担忧。孟加拉国是 H&M、Zara、沃尔玛和 Primark 等品牌的主要供应商，目前正处于春季和夏季出口订单生产周期的关键时刻。
工人要求将最低月工资从 12,500 塔卡提高到 30,000 塔卡（合 308 新元），他们在主要制造区封锁道路、破坏工厂并与警察发生冲突，导致 679 家工厂停产。
孟加拉国是仅次于中国的全球第二大服装出口国，成衣行业占该南亚国家出口收入的80%以上。它雇用了约 400 万工人，约占经济产出的 10%。
为了化解危机，政府于 11 月 1 日成立了一个由六名成员组成的工资委员会，以审查工人的要求，这些要求在持续的通货膨胀和生活成本上升的情况下得到了加强。
警方表示，在抗议者向警察投掷砖块和石块后，他们使用催泪瓦斯驱散了试图封锁达卡道路的制衣工人。据报道，首都郊区的两个制造中心阿苏利亚和加济布尔也发生了骚乱。
警方和行业官员表示，抗议者放火焚烧了一辆警车，并破坏了一些工厂。
11 月 2 日，孟加拉国加济布尔，警察与制衣工人发生冲突，一辆警车受损。
冲突发生在 11 月 1 日抗议和工厂关闭之后，工人们继续要求提高工资并解决就业不满。
“孟加拉国是世界上服装工资最低的国家之一，”孟加拉国服装和产业工人联合会秘书长、工资委员会工人代表巴布尔·阿赫特 (Babul Akhter) 说。
“如果工厂主无法向工人支付适当的工资，他们应该与国际买家谈判更好的价格。他们不能依靠工资过低的工人来开展业务。”
工厂主表示，该行业面临成本上升、中东冲突导致的能源市场不确定性以及主要出口市场需求放缓的问题。
孟加拉国服装制造商和出口商协会主席马哈茂德·哈桑·汗 (Mahmud Hasan Khan) 表示，骚乱期间约有 20 至 25 家工厂遭到破坏，一家皮革制品工厂的办公室也遭到袭击。
他说：“如果这种情况继续下去，工厂一再被迫关闭，我们将别无选择，只能援引‘不工作，不付工资’的规定。”
2026 年 11 月 2 日，达卡举行要求提高最低工资的抗议活动，警方人员拘留了一名制衣工人。
内政部长萨拉胡丁·艾哈迈德警告要采取强有力的行动：“那些以劳工抗议为幌子，损害工人利益并试图破坏国家稳定的人将受到坚决打击。”

Bangladesh garment factories shut again as wage protests turn violent | The Straits Times
Bangladesh garment factories shut again as wage protests turn violent
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Police personnel fire tear gas shells as garment workers block a road demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Published Nov 03, 2026, 01:05 AM
Updated Nov 03, 2026, 01:16 AM
DHAKA - Bangladesh’s garment factories briefly resumed operations on Nov 2 after a widespread shutdown a day earlier, but fresh clashes between workers and police forced hundreds of plants to suspend production again.
The unrest has raised concerns over shipment delays and buyer confidence in Bangladesh, a key supplier to brands including H&M, Zara, Walmart and Primark, at a critical point in the production cycle for spring and summer export orders.
Workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (S$308), up from 12,500 taka, blocked roads, vandalised factories and clashed with police across major manufacturing districts, prompting 679 factories to halt production.
Bangladesh is the world’s second-largest garment exporter after China and the ready-made garment sector accounts for more than 80% of the South Asian nation’s export earnings. It employs about 4 million workers and accounts for roughly 10% of economic output.
In a bid to defuse the crisis, the government on Nov 1 formed a six-member wage board to review workers’ demands, which have gained momentum amid persistent inflation and rising living costs.
Police said they used tear gas to disperse garment workers attempting to block roads in Dhaka after protesters hurled bricks and stones at officers. Unrest was also reported in Ashulia and Gazipur, two manufacturing hubs on the outskirts of the capital.
Police and industry officials said protesters set fire to a police vehicle and vandalised a number of factories.
A damaged police vehicle after a clash between police and garment workers in Gazipur, Bangladesh, on Nov 2.
The clashes follow the Nov 1 protests and factory closures, with workers continuing to demand higher wages and the resolution of employment grievances.
“Bangladesh has among the lowest garment wages in the world,” said Babul Akhter, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garment and Industrial Workers Federation and a workers’ representative on the wage board.
“If factory owners cannot pay workers properly, they should negotiate better prices with international buyers. They cannot build a business on the backs of underpaid workers.”
Factory owners said the industry faces higher costs, energy market uncertainty linked to conflict in the Middle East and slowing demand in key export markets.
Mahmud Hasan Khan, president of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, said around 20 to 25 factories were vandalised during the unrest and the office of a leather goods factory was also attacked.
“If this continues and factories are repeatedly forced to shut, we will have no option but to invoke the ‘no work, no pay’ provision,” he said.
Police personnel detain a garment worker during a protest demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka on Nov 2, 2026.
Home Affairs Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warned of robust action: “Those acting against workers’ interests under the guise of labour protests and attempting to destabilise the country will be dealt with firmly,” he said.
Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka, said that workers’ demands were understandable given high inflation and said there could be further unrest.
However, a substantial wage increase could raise production costs, squeeze profit margins and weaken Bangladesh’s price competitiveness, he said.
“A phased wage adjustment, improved productivity and fairer pricing from international buyers are essential to balancing workers’ welfare with industrial sustainability,” he said. REUTERS

北京11月2日电中国外交部长王毅周一在北京分别会见伊朗和沙特国家安全官员时表示，中东冲突各方应集中精力政治解决，而不是再次诉诸武力。
迫切希望在中东发挥更大外交作用的中国还宣布其特使将于本月访问伊朗、阿曼和沙特阿拉伯。
据中国官方通讯社新华社报道，王告诉伊朗最高国家安全委员会副秘书阿里·巴盖里·卡尼，对话和谈判是解决该地区冲突的途径。
王毅还表示，中方支持伊朗的主权和安全。
在与沙特阿拉伯国家安全顾问穆萨德·本·穆罕默德·艾班会谈后，王毅表示，地区局势“再次走到了战争与和平之间的关键十字路口”。
他表示，中方“希望各方通过对话谈判化解分歧、结束敌对行动，维护地区能源和航道安全”。
中国外交部称，艾班转交了沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼致中国国家主席习近平的信。
目前尚不清楚伊朗和沙特官员在北京是否有任何接触。
此前，习近平对阿曼领导人海赛姆·本·塔里克·赛义德表示，中东和海湾地区不应成为大国竞争的战场。
在随后的联合声明中，苏丹表示，阿曼支持中国对中东的和平建议，并期待北京在实现持久稳定方面发挥“更大作用”。路透社

BEIJING, Nov 2 - Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, in separate meetings with Iranian and Saudi national security officials in Beijing on Monday, said all parties in the Middle East conflict should focus on political solutions rather than resorting to arms again.
China, which is pressing for a bigger diplomatic role in the Middle East, also announced that its special envoy would visit Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month.
Wang told Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, that dialogue and negotiation were the way to resolve conflicts in the region, according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
Wang also said China supported Iran's sovereignty and security.
After talks with the national security adviser of Saudi Arabia, Musaed bin Mohammed Al-Aiban, Wang said the regional situation "has again reached a critical crossroads between war and peace."
China "hopes that all parties can resolve differences and end hostilities through dialogue and negotiations, and safeguard the region's energy and shipping lane security", he said.
Al-Aiban passed on a letter from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman addressed to Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.
It was not immediately clear whether the Iranian and Saudi officials had any contact with each other in Beijing.
Earlier, Xi told Omani leader Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said that the Middle East and Gulf region should not become a battleground for great-power rivalry.
In a joint statement that followed, the sultan said Oman supported Chinese peace proposals for the Middle East, and looked forward to a "greater role" by Beijing in achieving lasting stability. REUTERS

summary: 中国敏感问题下的美国-东盟防务框架海峡时报 新加坡将在地区敏感性中引导“互惠互利”的美国-东盟防务框架 立即注册：了解亚洲快速发展的发展 国防部长陈振声（右）于 10 月 28 日在菲律宾宿务正式从菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗手中接任 2027 年东盟国防部长会议主席。2026 年 11 月 2 日发布， 06:20 PM 更新于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，08:58 PM 新加坡将在 2027 年帮助塑造“互惠互利”的美国-东盟防务框架，因为它
content:
中国敏感问题下的美国-东盟防务框架海峡时报
新加坡将在地区敏感性中引导“互利”的美国-东盟防务框架
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
10月28日，国防部长陈振声（右）在菲律宾宿雾正式接替菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗担任2027年东盟防长会议主席。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 2 日 下午 06:20
更新于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，晚上 08:58
新加坡将在 2027 年担任 ADMM 主席国，帮助塑造“互惠互利”的美国-东盟防务框架。该计划旨在深化安全关系，而不迫使东盟选边站。
美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯提议加强海上合作、训练和互操作性。马来西亚、泰国和菲律宾欢迎美国加强参与，但都强调东盟的团结和对中国的谨慎态度。
分析人士表示，该框架可能会侧重于海上安全和能力建设，而不是集体防御。新加坡必须平衡美国与东盟成员国不同观点的关系以及中国紧张局势恶化的风险。
马尼拉 — — 新加坡将与华盛顿和其他东南亚国家合作，在 2027 年制定“互利”的美国-东盟防务合作框架，但强调这将与其他主要伙伴的现有防务安排一起推进。
新加坡国防部（MINDEF）在回应《海峡时报》有关该倡议的询问时发表上述评论，该倡议是美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯（Pete Hegseth）在10月28日的东盟国防部长会议（ADMM）上提出的。
作为 2027 年 ADMM 主席国，新加坡“期待推动”美国的提议。
外交部表示：“新加坡将与美国和其他东盟成员国合作，制定互利框架，让各方共同应对共同的挑战和关切。”
国防部补充说，拟议的框架将是东盟与其外部伙伴接触的几项举措之一，反映了该组织对开放和包容的地区安全架构的长期承诺。
声明称：“新加坡期待与东盟成员国和我们的+伙伴合作，加强防务合作并应对共同的安全挑战。”
国防部还指出，现有的部长级会议、与中国、印度、俄罗斯和美国的海上演习，以及涉及中国、韩国和新西兰的能力建设活动，称这些“补充了ADMM和ADMM+，并重申了东盟主导的地区安全架构的开放性和包容性”。
华盛顿尚未阐明防务框架的细节，但该倡议预计将于 2027 年形成，届时东盟和美国将庆祝建交 50 周年。
该提议出台之际，东南亚各国政府寻求深化与华盛顿的安全合作，同时又不被进一步卷入与北京的战略竞争。
菲律宾是美国的条约盟友，在南海与北京面临海上对抗，菲律宾一直明确表示华盛顿对地区安全的重要性。
菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗在 ADMM 上表示，“美国的强大存在对于东南亚和更广泛的印太地区的和平与稳定是必要的”。
泰国对该提案表示欢迎，认为这是积极的一步，但表示它必须补充现有的 ASEA

【原文 English Original】
US-ASEAN defence framework amid China sensitivities | The Straits Times
Singapore to steer ‘mutually beneficial’ US-ASEAN defence framework amid regional sensitivities
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing (right) formally took over the chairmanship of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting for 2027 from his Philippine counterpart Gilberto Teodoro Jr in Cebu, the Philippines, on Oct 28.
Published Nov 02, 2026, 06:20 PM
Updated Nov 02, 2026, 08:58 PM
Singapore will help shape a “mutually beneficial” US-ASEAN defence framework in 2027, as it chairs ADMM next year. The plan aims to deepen security ties without forcing ASEAN to choose sides.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth proposed closer maritime cooperation, training and interoperability. Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines welcomed stronger US engagement, but all stressed ASEAN unity and caution on China.
Analysts said the framework will likely focus on maritime security and capacity-building, not collective defence. Singapore must balance US ties with ASEAN members’ differing views and the risk of worsening China tensions.
MANILA – Singapore will work with Washington and other South-east Asian countries to develop a “mutually beneficial” US-ASEAN defence cooperation framework in 2027, but has stressed that this will be pursued alongside existing defence arrangements with other key partners.
Singapore’s Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) made the comments in response to queries from The Straits Times about the initiative, which was proposed by US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) on Oct 28.
As chair of the ADMM in 2027, Singapore “looks forward to facilitating” the US proposal.
“Singapore will work with the US and other ASEAN member states to develop a mutually beneficial framework for all parties to work together in response to shared challenges and concerns,” the ministry said.
MINDEF added that the proposed framework would be one of several initiatives through which ASEAN engages its external partners, reflecting the grouping’s longstanding commitment to an open and inclusive regional security architecture.
“Singapore looks forward to working with ASEAN Member States and our Plus partners to strengthen defence cooperation and address shared security challenges,” it said.
MINDEF also pointed to existing ministers’ meetings, maritime exercises with China, India, Russia and the US, as well as capacity-building activities involving China, South Korea and New Zealand, saying these “complement the ADMM and ADMM-Plus and reaffirm the open and inclusive nature of the ASEAN-led regional security architecture”.
Washington has yet to spell out the details of the defence framework, but the initiative is expected to take shape in 2027, when ASEAN and the US mark 50 years of relations.
The proposal comes as South-east Asian governments seek to deepen security cooperation with Washington without being drawn further into its strategic rivalry with Beijing.
The Philippines, a US treaty ally facing maritime confrontations with Beijing in the South China Sea, has been unequivocal about Washington’s importance to regional security.
Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr said at the ADMM that a “robust US presence was necessary for peace and stability in South-east Asia and in the broader Indo-Pacific region”.
Thailand welcomed the proposal as a positive step, but said it must complement existing ASEAN-led mechanisms and avoid worsening strategic competition.
“It should not lead to further divisions or exacerbate strategic competition in the region,” a Thai Foreign Ministry spokesperson told ST.
Malaysia also welcomed stronger US engagement, with Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled Nordin saying Kuala Lumpur looks forward to the framework in 2027.
“Our approach has never been about choosing sides. It is about preserving the peace and stability that have allowed our region to prosper,” he said in his ADMM remarks in Cebu.
Indonesia has not publicly responded to the proposal, although Deputy Defence Minister Richard T.H. Tampubolon stressed ASEAN unity and centrality during the Cebu meetings.
Analysts interviewed by ST said the initiative would likely focus on maritime security, military training and capacity-building rather than resemble a collective defence arrangement.
Gregory Poling, director of the Southeast Asia Program and Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington DC, said the framework could consolidate existing US security programmes in the region.
“I think the best guess is that this would knit together a lot of the programmes focused on capacity building, arms sales and arms transfers and training that have been going on for years,” he said.
Poling said the proposal could also reassure regional governments concerned about Washington’s long-term commitment. “Clearly what everybody wanted from Secretary Hegseth was reassurance about US staying power (in ASEAN),” he said.
Political scientist Aries Arugay, visiting senior fellow at Singapore’s ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute, welcomed the proposal as a concrete opportunity to deepen Washington’s engagement with ASEAN as a grouping.
“This reflects something concrete that could bind the US towards the region,” he said, adding that the initiative would need sufficient resources and follow-through to succeed.
The US says ships and submarines trump summits. South-east Asia politely says ‘no’
Hegseth hails Asian partners for boosting security spending; omits Taiwan in roll call
Collin Koh, a senior fellow at Singapore’s S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, said Singapore’s close defence relationship with the US puts it in a sensitive position as incoming ADMM chair.
While Singapore considers the US vital to regional security, Koh said it would be cautious about appearing to promote an arrangement other ASEAN members could perceive as collective defence or an effort to contain China.
He said the framework would likely be scaled back to accommodate ASEAN’s differing priorities and military capabilities.
“Potentially you might find yourself having to cater to the lowest common denominator,” he said, noting that ASEAN’s defence cooperation with external powers has traditionally been built around overlapping partnerships instead of exclusive security commitments.
Singapore Defence Minister Chan Chun Sing said in Cebu on Oct 29 that ASEAN needed mechanisms that could accommodate different security priorities and capabilities.
“There is a diversity of aspirations, a diversity of capabilities around the world, and we will need a mechanism that allows us to build an overlapping network of bilateral and plurilateral ties in order to advance our shared interests,” he said.
Singapore formally took over the ADMM chairmanship for 2027 from the Philippines during the Cebu meetings, with Chan pledging to work closely with ASEAN member-states and their external partners to address evolving security challenges.
While ASEAN-wide cooperation could include maritime domain awareness and humanitarian assistance, more sophisticated military activities would likely remain bilateral or involve smaller groups.
“When it comes to more substantial operational capabilities, say, engaging in joint training that has a warfighting dimension, maybe not ASEAN. I don’t think ASEAN will engage in that,” said S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies’ Koh.
Koh added that differing military equipment and levels of interoperability would make it difficult to develop advanced joint capabilities across all 11 members.
China cries foul as tensions with Manila flare at ASEAN defence talks
ASEAN defence ministers reaffirm commitment to free flow of trade through international corridors
China did not send Defence Minister Dong Jun to the ADMM-Plus in Cebu but was instead represented at a lower level, amid heightened tensions with Manila over the South China Sea.
Poling said Beijing’s absence reflected deteriorating China-Philippine relations, while Washington’s proposed framework could raise wider concerns over ASEAN being drawn into strategic competition.
“There are obvious practical benefits if this unlocks more US funding, more US training, more interoperability around the region,” he said.
“The trade-off is, is this seen as a US imposition or is it seen as ASEAN being roped into a US-China competition?”
Even maritime domain awareness, a seemingly practical area of cooperation, would be difficult to separate from concerns over China’s activities at sea, he added.
Arugay offered a more optimistic assessment. He argued that deeper US engagement could help South-east Asian governments balance China’s growing influence without abandoning their relationships with Beijing.
“These countries will hedge, and any signal from the US balances off China’s overwhelming presence and their engagement with China,” he said.
Mara Cepeda is Philippines correspondent at The Straits Times.

title: Needless provocation? Japanese blockbuster hit Vivant portrays China as sadistic villain
zh_title: 无谓的挑衅？日本大片《Vivant》将中国描绘成残暴的恶棍
summary: 日本谍战剧《Vivant》引发中国强烈反对海峡时报 不必要的挑衅？日本大片《维旺》将中国描绘成残暴的恶棍。一部虚构的间谍剧与现实世界的地缘政治发生碰撞，引发了一场跨境风暴，触动了中国的敏感神经。立即注册：深入了解亚洲快速发展的趋势 TBS 旗舰剧《Vivant》的剧照，在北京因其对中国特工的无情和残暴的描述而受到冒犯后，该剧成为媒体风暴的中心。发布于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，晚上 09:15 更新于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，晚上 11:06
content:
日本谍战剧《Vivant》引发中国强烈反对海峡时报
无谓的挑衅？日本大片《Vivant》将中国描绘成残暴的恶棍
一部虚构的间谍剧与现实世界的地缘政治发生碰撞，引发了一场跨境风暴，触动了中国的敏感神经。
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
这是 TBS 旗舰剧《维万特》的剧照，在北京对其对中国特工的残酷和虐待行为的描述感到愤怒后，该剧成为媒体风暴的中心。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 2 日 晚上 09:15
更新于 2026 年 11 月 2 日 11:06
日本电视剧《维旺》将中国特工描绘成残酷的酷刑者，引发了中国的愤怒。
在中国官方媒体称其为“认知战”以及北京指责日本存在反华偏见后，这场争吵愈演愈烈。
专家警告说，流行文化对公众对外交事务看法的影响不容忽视。
东京 — — 日本卖座电视剧《维旺》于 11 月 1 日播出，一集以非传统的免责声明开场，试图平息因该剧将中国政府特工描绘成冷酷无情、虐待狂的施虐者而引发的争议。
东京广播公司 (TBS) 周日旗舰系列节目倒数第二集开头的屏幕通知中写道：“我们绝对无意煽动国家之间的暴力或冲突。”
“该剧纯属虚构，与任何真实的人物、组织、事件、历史事件没有任何关系。剧中对国家和地区的描述纯属虚构。”
这部精彩的间谍惊悚片在主创们自己制造的地缘政治阴云下，即将迎来 11 月 8 季的大结局。这部作品引发了北京方面的强烈谴责，而Hello Kitty的创作者日本企业巨头三丽鸥也取消了与该剧的官方商品合作。
对于一部在海外拍摄的电影场景（包括蒙古和阿塞拜疆等国家）、错综复杂的情节以及由日本最有票房收入的明星组成的演员阵容的高预算剧集来说，这是一个不幸的干扰。
据这位记者报道，日本各地有数千万人每周日收看节目或通过国内流媒体平台观看节目。
《Vivant》讲述了野木佑介（堺正人饰）的故事，他是一名笨手笨脚的贸易公司工薪族，在日本自卫队 (JSDF) 内部的秘密情报机构“Beppan”中过着精英特工的双重生活。该节目的热烈反响甚至一度促使防卫大臣小泉进二郎公开否认该部队的存在。
乃木与警察督察野崎守（阿部宽饰）以及乃木的养弟诺科尔（已解散男孩乐队岚的二宫一成饰）一起工作，后者是来自虚构的中亚“巴尔卡共和国”的神秘恐怖组织 Tent 的头目。
第一季共 10 集，于 2023 年播出，目前在 Netflix 上全球播出，在虚构的巴尔卡地区保持地缘政治中立。
第二季于 7 月首播，但在国际流媒体平台上仍无法播放，该剧通过明确将中国作为对手，实现了当代东亚地缘政治的重大飞跃。虽然阿塞拜疆和泰国等其他现实世界国家也出现在剧中，但中国被列为敌对国家。
明确点名中国的决定是否是由东京现在例行将北京列为最高领导人的方式推动的？

【原文 English Original】
Japanese spy drama Vivant sparks China backlash | The Straits Times
Needless provocation? Japanese blockbuster hit Vivant portrays China as sadistic villain
A cross-border storm breaks out as a fictional espionage drama collides with real-world geopolitics, touching off Chinese sensitivities.
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The production title still of TBS flagship drama Vivant, which is at the centre of a media storm after Beijing took offence at its ruthless and sadistic portrayal of Chinese agents.
Published Nov 02, 2026, 09:15 PM
Updated Nov 02, 2026, 11:06 PM
Japanese drama Vivant sparked anger in China after it portrayed Chinese agents as brutal torturers.
The row grew after Chinese state media called it “cognitive warfare” and Beijing accused Japan of anti-China bias.
Experts caution that pop culture's impact on public perception of foreign affairs cannot be ignored.
TOKYO – The Nov 1 episode of Japanese blockbuster TV drama Vivant opened with an unconventional disclaimer, an attempt to defuse a controversy over the production’s portrayal of Chinese government agents as ruthless, sadistic torturers.
“We have absolutely no intention of promoting violence or conflict between nations,” read the on-screen notice at the start of the penultimate episode of the Tokyo Broadcasting System (TBS) Sunday flagship series.
“This drama is fiction, and has no relation whatsoever to any real people, organisations, events, or historical occurrences. The depictions of countries and regions in the drama are fictional creations,” it said.
The high-octane spy thriller is hurtling towards its Nov 8 season finale under a geopolitical cloud of its creators’ own making. The production has triggered fierce condemnation from Beijing while Japanese corporate giant Sanrio, the creators of Hello Kitty, has axed an official merchandise collaboration with the show.
This is an unfortunate distraction for a high-budget series that has been extremely entertaining with cinematic scenes filmed overseas including countries like Mongolia and Azerbaijan, labyrinthine plot twists, and an ensemble cast of Japan’s most bankable stars.
Tens of millions across Japan tune in every Sunday or catch up via domestic streaming platforms, this correspondent included.
Vivant follows Yusuke Nogi (Masato Sakai), a bumbling trading firm salaryman who leads a double life as an elite operative in “Beppan”, a clandestine intelligence outfit buried within the Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF). The show’s feverish reception even once prompted Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi to publicly deny the unit’s existence.
Nogi works alongside police inspector Mamoru Nozaki (Hiroshi Abe) and Nogi’s foster brother Nokor (Kazunari Ninomiya of defunct boy band Arashi), a leading figure in the enigmatic terrorist syndicate Tent which hails from the fictional Central Asian “Republic of Balka”.
Season 1, a 10-part series that aired in 2023 and is currently available globally on Netflix, remained geopolitically neutral within the make-believe Balka.
Season 2, which premiered in July and remains unavailable on international streaming platforms, made the fateful leap into contemporary East Asian geopolitics by casting China explicitly as the antagonist. While other real-world nations like Azerbaijan and Thailand also feature in the drama, China is singled out as the hostile power.
Was the decision to explicitly name China driven by how Tokyo now routinely names Beijing as its top security threat? Even so, had scriptwriters stopped at merely identifying China as a threat, the drama could have passed as pure fiction.
The bone of contention was the scenes of interrogation carried out by fictional Chinese intelligence agency “Xinxi”, featuring captured Japanese agents subjected to graphic brutal torture that includes severing of fingers and stabs to the abdomen. And at least one scene suggests sexual abuse, although this is not explicit and left open to viewer interpretation.
While creative liberties must be protected, this should not come with a blank cheque at the expense of social sensitivities. It is here that Vivant crossed out-of-bounds markers and it is therefore unsurprising that Beijing has reacted with fury, with Chinese state media labelling the drama as “cognitive poisoning” and “cognitive warfare”.
One complaint centres on what critics describe as “historical inversion”, projecting torture methods historically inflicted by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II – not just in China, but also across the Korean Peninsula and South-east Asia – onto modern-day Chinese figures.
This grievance is justified, when seen against how Japanese history education tends to gloss over Japan’s wartime atrocities even while acknowledging the country’s role as an aggressor that lost the war. Might the scriptwriters simply have been unaware of how close their fiction comes to historical reality?
Many Japanese netizens also accuse Beijing of double standards, pointing to Chinese “hypocrisy”, given that China’s state-backed film industry routinely churns out patriotic blockbusters and anti-Japanese war epics. These include Unit 731 (2025), which graphically detailed the Imperial Japanese Army’s biological experimentation in Harbin.
Yet, no matter where one stands on WWII history, dramatising a war that ended 81 years ago with characters of a bygone era differs from portraying a contemporary neighbour as an active threat devoid of moral restraint.
The diplomatic fallout prompted TBS president Masamine Ryuho to emphasise at an Oct 28 news conference that Vivant is a “completely fictitious entertainment work” with “no intention of disparaging any specific country or hurting national sentiment”, adding that the broadcaster does not want to stoke international enmity.
China was unconvinced. A day later, Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular press briefing: “This television drama once again reveals the persistent existence inside Japan of a force that seeks to use cultural products to vilify and smear China and spread anti-Chinese sentiment.”
Even an offhand remark by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, under whom bilateral ties have chilled following her November 2025 statement in Parliament suggesting JSDF mobilisation if China should invade the self-ruling Taiwan, became entangled in the dispute.
Takaichi had told a parliamentary committee on Oct 14 that she was recording weekly episodes of Vivant, hoping to binge-watch them over the year-end holidays. Beijing would come to seize upon this remark as high-level endorsement for “anti-China propaganda”.
The corporate fallout followed, with Sanrio scrapping its merchandise collaboration and the company’s Shanghai subsidiary apologising on Weibo, stating that the drama contained expressions “inconsistent with our corporate philosophy” of harmony and peace.
It is easy to view Beijing’s outrage as calculated political theatre, given its own track record of state-backed patriotic cinema.
Beijing raps Japan drama Vivant over violent portrayal of Chinese agents
Demon Slayer movie screening not extended in China amid dispute with Japan
Moreover, as Daito Bunka University professor Tsuyoshi Nojima noted on news aggregator site NewsPicks, Vivant’s portrayal of Chinese intelligence is hardly a masterclass in sinister propaganda. Naming a top-secret spy agency “Xinxi”, literally the Chinese word for “information”, is laughably unsubtle.
Furthermore, casting Japanese actors as elite Chinese spooks and having them deliver heavily accented Mandarin, which I found difficult to understand without subtitles, immediately shatters any sense of realism.
Yet pop culture does not exist in a geopolitical vacuum. Former diplomat Masaru Sato cautioned in the Asahi Shimbun that even in fiction, “the impact of subculture on public perception of foreign affairs cannot be ignored”.
Spy fiction thrives on high-stakes conflict, and every espionage thriller needs an adversary. But casting a real-life, close neighbour as a brutal torturer was entirely avoidable.
Had the antagonists remained rooted in an imaginary realm, or even been styled as a rogue syndicate rather than a state-backed agency, Vivant could have delivered suspense without throwing to the wind geopolitical common sense.
Walter Sim is Japan correspondent at The Straits Times. Based in Tokyo, he writes about political, economic and socio-cultural issues.

Snap settles lawsuit accusing platform of fueling teen depression and eating disorders
Snap has reached a settlement in a lawsuit brought by two teenagers who accused the company of designing its platform to be addictive and contributing to their depression, anxiety, and eating disorders, as first reported by Reuters. The plaintiffs had previously reached settlements with Meta, TikTok, and YouTube.
The trial was set to be Snap’s first in a broader wave of litigation over social media’s impact on young users. The company had already settled its other cases scheduled for trial. Snap CEO Evan Spiegel was expected to take the stand.
The plaintiffs said they started using YouTube as young as age 3 and other social media platforms at around age 9. They said they developed compulsive usage habits, which they attributed to features such as autoplay and infinite scrolling.
“The Parties are pleased to have been able to resolve this matter in an amicable manner,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “We’ve built safeguards, launched safety tutorials, and partnered with experts and because safety is never finished, we remain committed to continually strengthening the safety, privacy, and well-being of our community.”
Social media giants are facing thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts over claims that they knowingly designed their platforms to hook young users and fuel a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression, and suicide.

据未透露姓名的消息人士称，演习计划持续到周五，将使用空军的主要战斗机——F-16V、幻影 2000-5 和本土防御战斗机（IDF）来测试飞行员的空对空、空对海和空对地作战技能。

与往年一样，空军还将评选不同类别的王牌飞行员，包括空战和精确飞行。
消息人士补充说，天龙演习还将包括地面后勤保障演习，并测试空军与陆军、海军以及信息、通信和电子部队司令部的联合作战能力。

Mirage 2000 fighter jets are pictured at the Hsinchu Air Base in the CNA file photo.
Taipei, Nov. 1 (CNA) Taiwan's Air Force is scheduled to begin its annual Tien Lung, or "Sky Dragon," drills on Monday to test pilots' combat skills and ground-based logistical support, a military source told CNA on Sunday.
The drills are scheduled to run through Friday and will test pilots' air-to-air, air-to-sea, and air-to-ground combat skills using the Air Force's main fighter aircraft -- F-16Vs, Mirage 2000-5s, and Indigenous Defense Fighters (IDFs) -- according to the unnamed source.
The exercises will focus on aerial interceptions and the use of the aerial gunnery target system (AGTS). They will also simulate pilots scrambling their aircraft at short notice, identifying targets, firing missiles at them, and conducting mock "dogfights" with enemy aircraft, the source said.
As in previous years, the Air Force will also select flying aces in different categories, including aerial combat and precision.
The source added that the Tien Lung exercises will also include ground-based logistical support drills and test the Air Force's joint operational capabilities with the Army, Navy, and Information, Communications and Electronic Force Command.

PRAGUE, Nov 2 - A Prague court ruled on Monday that a Chinese man suspected of espionage in the Czech Republic was not guilty and ordered his release, the news agency CTK reported.
The man, who had worked in Prague as a journalist, was arrested in January, accused of building up connections with Czech officials and collecting information that may be harmful to the Czech Republic.
But a court ruled that his activity was not criminal, CTK said.
A state attorney appealed both the ruling and the release from custody, sending the case to a higher court, CTK said. Yang Yiming, who had denied wrongdoing, was not ordered to remain in the country, but his lawyer said he was not planning to leave at the moment, it said.
Yang, who Czech media said was a reporter for a Communist Party-affiliated newspaper, had been charged with conducting "unauthorised activity for a foreign power".
Chinese authorities had demanded the release of the man while commenting on the June detention of a Czech citizen in China.
The Czech man has been held in China on suspicion of national security offences, Chinese officials said.
Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka has said the cases were unrelated.
Beijing and Prague have signalled a warming of diplomatic ties in recent months after tensions under the previous Czech administration due to its strong ties with Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by China.
The Czech government in power since last December has sought a more pragmatic relationship with Beijing. REUTERS

content:
台湾10月制造业活动扩张但势头放缓 - 焦点台湾
台湾10月制造业活动扩张但势头减弱

中新社台北11月2日电 中华经济研究院(CIER)周一表示，10月份台湾制造业活动仍处于扩张状态，但由于衡量该行业活动的指数环比下降，包括新订单、生产和就业在内的所有五个主要分项指数均下降，增长动力减弱。
台湾领先的经济智库之一CIER援引数据称，10月份制造业采购经理人指数(PMI)环比下降0.9点至62.5。与此同时，PMI 连续 13 个月保持扩张。
10月份服务业非制造业指数（NMI）也较上月下降1.5点至55.4，但连续第20个月保持扩张状态。
PMI和NMI读数高于50表明扩张，低于50则表明收缩。
CIER表示，10月份，新订单、生产、就业、供应商交货和库存分类指数均较9月份分别下降0.4、0.9、1.3、0.2和1.4点至63.2、64.7、56.3、68.4和60.0点。
CIER 补充称，新订单分类指数连续第二个月下降。
然而，CIER表示，未来六个月商业前景分类指数较9月上升0.3点至10月的61.7，标志着该分类指数连续10个月保持在60以上。
CIER总裁连贤明告诉记者，全球人工智能发展出现放缓迹象，很大程度上是由于缺乏关键零部件，特别是存储芯片和基板，导致交付推迟。
此外，连恩表示，市场密切关注大规模的人工智能投资能否产生足够的回报。
他指出，尽管台湾 10 月份 PMI 较 9 月份有所下降，但这可归因于势头放缓，而不是经济气候逆转。
CIER副院长陈信宏回应连连表示，人工智能和其他行业一样，有起有落。
六大行业中，仅电力电气设备、交通运输设备等行业分类指数上涨，化工/生物、电子/光电、食品/纺织、基础原材料等行业分类指数均下跌。六大产业均在扩张。
CIER表示，虽然第四季度国内消费保持强劲，提振了零售销售和旅游业，但由于全球股市波动，金融业的势头放缓，给10月份更广泛的服务业带来压力。
CIER补充称，10月份，NMI四大分项指数中的三个——商业活动、就业和供应商交付——分别较上月下降3.0、2.3和0.7点至54.7、54.1和56.0，而只有新订单分项指数保持不变。
未来六个月商业前景分类指数也较 9 月下降 1.6 点，至 10 月的 56.2，但连续 10 个月保持扩张。

Taiwan's October manufacturing activity in expansion but momentum eases
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 2 (CNA) Taiwan's manufacturing activity remained in expansion in October, although growth momentum weakened as the index measuring activity in the sector fell from a month earlier with all five major subindexes, including new orders, production and employment, on the decline, the Chung-Hua Institution for Economic Research (CIER) said Monday.
Citing data, CIER, one of Taiwan's leading economic think tanks, said the October purchasing managers' index (PMI) in the manufacturing sector fell 0.9 points from a month earlier to 62.5. At the same time, the PMI remained in expansion for a 13th consecutive month.
The non-manufacturing index (NMI) for the service sector also fell 1.5 points from a month earlier to 55.4 in October but remained in expansion mode for a 20th consecutive month.
PMI and NMI readings above 50 indicate expansion, while those below 50 show contraction.
In October, the subindexes for new orders, production, employment, supplier deliveries and inventories all moved lower by 0.4, 0.9, 1.3, 0.2 and 1.4 points, respectively, from September to 63.2, 64.7, 56.3, 68.4 and 60.0 points, CIER said.
The subindex for new orders recorded its second consecutive monthly decline, CIER added.
However, the subindex for business outlook over the next six months moved higher by 0.3 points from September to 61.7 in October, marking the 10th consecutive month that the subindex has stayed above 60, CIER said.
CIER President Lien Hsien-ming (連賢明) told reporters that global AI development showed signs of moderating largely due to a lack of crucial components, particularly memory chips and substrates, which postponed deliveries.
In addition, Lien said the market has paid close attention to whether massive AI investments will generate adequate returns.
Although Taiwan's October PMI fell from September that can be attributed to slowing momentum not an economic climate reversal, he noted.
Echoing Lien, CIER Vice President Chen Shin-Horng (陳信宏) said AI, like any other industry, has ups and downs.
Among the six major industries, only the electricity and electrical equipment and transportation equipment sectors saw increases in their subindexes, while those for chemical/biotech, electronics/optoelectronics, food/textile and basic raw material industries all moved lower. The six industries were all in expansion.
While domestic consumption stayed solid in the fourth quarter, boosting retail sales and tourism, momentum in the financial sector slowed amid volatility in global equity markets, weighing on the broader services sector in October, CIER said.
In October, three of the four major subindexes of the NMI -- business activity, employment and supplier deliveries -- fell 3.0, 2.3 and 0.7 points, respectively, from a month earlier to 54.7, 54.1 and 56.0, while only the subindex on new orders stayed unchanged, CIER added.
The subindex on business outlook over the next six months also fell 1.6 points from September to 56.2 in October but stayed in expansion for a 10th straight month.

content:
消息人士称，美国枪支通过香港网络走私到朝鲜海峡时报
消息人士称，美国枪支通过香港网络走私到朝鲜

这些武器与外交官的物品一起装载到一艘名为“Sun Rich”的货船上。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，晚上 10:25
更新于 2026 年 11 月 2 日，晚上 10:38
据多位知情人士透露，包括一名中国公民在内的一个以香港自由贸易港为基地的私人网络在涉及朝鲜的武器走私行动中发挥了关键作用，导致一名中国男子于 2024 年在美国被捕。
该网络采用了精心策划的计划，将从美国运往香港的枪支运输到香港，并将其藏在回国的朝鲜外交官的家庭物品中。据信，在国际社会监测非法向朝鲜运送武器的努力减弱的情况下，走私活动仍然活跃。
据美国检察官称，文胜华按照朝鲜官员的指示，于2023年12月将他在美国采购的枪支从加利福尼亚州长滩港运往香港。这些武器于2024年1月1日左右抵达香港，随后被运往朝鲜。
联合国安理会决议禁止向朝鲜出口武器。文于 2025 年 8 月被判刑。
据知情人士透露，来自香港的走私活动是由一名香港人领导的，他实际上控制着一家被指定为美国货物接收人的贸易公司。据报道，在 2023 年朝鲜驻香港总领事馆关闭后，他还签订了合同，负责运送朝鲜外交官的家庭物品回国。
据称，该男子等待2023年12月从美国运来的武器抵达香港，然后安排将它们与外交官的物品一起装上一艘当时悬挂塞拉利昂国旗、名为Sun Rich的货船。
这些武器被错误地宣称为“冰箱”和“厨房设备”。
此次诈骗利用了香港作为自由贸易港处理大量货物的相对简单的进出口程序，以及海关当局不会仔细检查含有外交官个人物品的货物的预期。
消息人士称，外交官们自己完全不知道这一计划。
消息人士称，参与走私活动的其他人包括一名实际上拥有这艘货船的台湾男子和一名实际上是一家航运公司经营者的中国男子。
消息人士称，该网络继续运营由四艘货船组成的船队。其最近的活动包括运输钢铁产品，而联合国安理会的制裁也禁止向朝鲜出口钢铁产品。该网络还可能计划将石油从马来西亚走私到朝鲜。
在俄罗斯否决延长其任期的决议后，负责监督对朝鲜制裁遵守情况的联合国安理会专家小组被迫于 2024 年 4 月停止运作。
该小组前成员 Katsuhisa Furukawa 检查了美国的起诉记录，并将其与《读卖新闻》提供的几份文件进行了交叉核对

Guns from US smuggled into North Korea by Hong Kong network, sources say | The Straits Times
Guns from US smuggled into North Korea by Hong Kong network, sources say
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The weapons were loaded alongside diplomats’ belongings onto a cargo ship that was named the Sun Rich.
Published Nov 02, 2026, 10:25 PM
Updated Nov 02, 2026, 10:38 PM
A network of private individuals, including a Chinese national, based in the free-trade port of Hong Kong played a key role in a weapons-smuggling operation involving North Korea that led to the arrest of a Chinese man in the US in 2024, according to multiple people familiar with the case.
The network used an elaborate scheme to transport firearms that had been shipped from the US to Hong Kong, concealing them among the household belongings of North Korean diplomats returning home. The smuggling operation is believed to still be active, amid weakened international efforts to monitor illicit arms shipments to North Korea.
According to US prosecutors, Shenghua Wen, acting on instructions from North Korean officials, shipped firearms he had procured in the US from the Port of Long Beach, California, to Hong Kong in December 2023. The weapons arrived in Hong Kong around Jan 1, 2024, and were subsequently transported to North Korea.
United Nations Security Council resolutions prohibit arms exports to North Korea. Wen was sentenced in August 2025.
According to people familiar with the operation, the smuggling effort from Hong Kong was led by a Hong Kong man who effectively controlled a trading company designated as the recipient of the shipment from the US. He had reportedly also been contracted to transport the household belongings of North Korean diplomats returning home, following the closure of North Korea’s Consulate General in Hong Kong in 2023.
The man is said to have waited for the weapons shipped from the US in December 2023 to arrive in Hong Kong, and then arranged for them to be loaded alongside the diplomats’ belongings onto a cargo ship that was named the Sun Rich and flying the flag of Sierra Leone at the time.
The weapons were falsely declared as being “refrigerators” and “kitchen equipment”.
The deception exploited Hong Kong’s relatively simple import and export procedures as a free-trade port handling enormous volumes of cargo, as well as the expectation that the customs authorities would not closely inspect shipments containing diplomats’ personal belongings.
The diplomats themselves were entirely unaware of the scheme, according to the sources.
Others involved in the smuggling operation included a Taiwanese man who effectively owned the cargo ship and a Chinese man who was the de facto operator of a shipping company, the sources said.
The network continues to operate a fleet of four cargo ships, according to the sources. Its recent activities have included shipments of iron and steel products, whose export to North Korea is also prohibited under UN Security Council sanctions. The network may also be planning to smuggle petroleum from Malaysia to North Korea.
The UN Security Council’s Panel of Experts, which monitored compliance with sanctions imposed on North Korea, was forced to cease operations at the end of April 2024, after Russia vetoed a resolution to extend its mandate.
Katsuhisa Furukawa, a former member of the panel, examined US prosecution records and cross-checked them against several documents provided to The Yomiuri Shimbun by people familiar with the smuggling operation.
Based on his analysis, Furukawa concluded that there were “substantial grounds to regard the accounts as reasonable and credible”.
The cargo ship used to smuggle the weapons has repeatedly sailed under different names and flags. It has also been confirmed that the vessel has repeatedly engaged in unusual behaviour, including switching off its automatic identification system, which transmits and receives information about a ship’s location and other data, after leaving Hong Kong and reaching waters around the Yellow Sea.
According to Furukawa, the vessel has “almost no record of calling at the ports it had declared as its destinations, including ports in South Korea”.
“The only plausible explanation is that the vessel has repeatedly made clandestine calls at North Korean ports,” Furukawa added.
He stressed that all UN member states, including China, must implement asset-freezing measures, including seizing the vessel, in accorfdance with Security Council resolutions. THE JAPAN NEWS/ASIA NEWS NETWORK

2 Hours to Freedom: Build a Job Hunt AI Agent with Claude
There are many groups promoting this event.
Our meetup group is participating by promoting this event.
This event is organized by Albert's List.
Attendees can be located anywhere in the world!
There is a cost to attend this event.
In order to attend, please register here:
https://www.eventbrite.com/e/2003644622001?aff=oddtdtcreator
Build an AI agent that job hunts while you sleep.
In this hands‑on session, you’ll use Claude to build a job hunt agent that actually saves you time instead of creating more busywork. You’ll learn how to set up focused channels for targeting roles, researching companies, and tailoring outreach, then wire in various APIs so your agent can pull fresh job postings and context on demand. We'll learn how to have a reusable channel setup and prompt patterns you can run weekly to keep your search organized, personalized, and mostly on autopilot.
Build an AI agent that job hunts while you sleep.
AI agents are an emerging way to automate parts of your job search, from sourcing roles to drafting outreach, so you spend less time grinding and more time in real conversations.
In this beta, hands‑on workshop, you’ll follow a guided build to assemble a prototype “Job Search Copilot” using Claude. Rather than promising a polished, one‑click agent, we’ll focus on helping you understand the building blocks: structuring prompts and tasks, wiring simple workflows, and tailoring behaviors for your role or niche.
Because tools and setups vary, not every participant will leave with a perfectly running agent in their own environment. Instead, you’ll leave with:
A concrete mental model of how AI agents support a job search.
A copy of the instructor’s working example project you can study and reuse.
Templates, code snippets, and a step‑by‑step guide you can revisit after the session to get your own version fully working.
No prior technical experience is required, but you should be comfortable installing software and copying commands. If you hit environment issues during the live session, we’ll provide ways to follow along using prepared checkpoints so you can still absorb the patterns and process.
This session will be recorded. All registrants receive:
Links to the example project.
Written setup instructions and troubleshooting tips.
Whether you’re a jobseeker, career coach, or a professional curious about operationalizing AI in your workflow, this workshop is designed to give you a realistic, experiment‑ready starting point, not a finished product.
A reusable blueprint for building simple AI agents with modern tools.
A prototype “Job Search Copilot” project (or access to a working example) that you can refine after the workshop.
Practical patterns you can extend to other use cases beyond job hunting.
Finally, this session will be recorded. If you sign up and cannot make it, a recording will be sent to you.

调查显示公众对台湾金融服务信心升至64.1%
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
台湾银行金融学院。 CNA档案照片
中新社台北11月2日电 台湾金融学院(TABF)周一表示，最新调查显示，64.1%的受访者对使用金融产品和服务有信心，而大学生越来越多地将投资视为省钱或对冲通胀的一种方式。
TABF 召开新闻发布会，发布两年一度的调查结果，今年的调查结合了公共金融行为的定量调查和探讨大学生如何进行投资的深度访谈。
调查发现，公众对金融产品和服务的信心从2024年的38.9%上升到今年的64.1%。调查还显示，86.5%的受访者可以轻松支付日常家庭开支，而51.6%的受访者有足够的储蓄来支付紧急情况下至少六个月的基本生活费用。
TABF主席雷仲达表示，公众信心的改善得益于人工智能需求的增长、台湾股市创历史新高以及实际GDP的高增长。
在财务风险方面，调查发现，72%的受访者会在紧急情况下向个人储蓄、家人或朋友寻求经济支持，低于之前调查的约80%。与此同时，更多受访者表示将出售股票或共同基金、以保单借款或申请银行贷款，利率分别上升3.8、5.2和10.6个百分点。
TABF管理团队成员郑翰表示，调查结果表明，人们对股票投资风险的警惕性降低，越来越多地将股票视为稳定的收入来源。
他建议人们保持足够的现金储蓄，以支付三到六个月的生活费用，并警告说，市场波动或低迷可能会迫使投资者低价出售股票并蒙受损失。
调查还发现，公众对避免金融诈骗的信心从2024年的65.7%上升到今年的73.8%。然而，70岁及以上的老年人仍然特别脆弱，与其他年龄组相比，他们对使用金融服务的信心较低，电子支付使用年龄也较低。
这张 CNA 档案照片中的一名银行员工协助客户操作 ATM 机（仅供说明）
对于年轻人，程说，许多大学生的投资动机是担心通货膨胀会侵蚀他们银行储蓄的价值，而家人、朋友和在线平台帮助塑造了他们的投资习惯和信心。
调查还警告说，虽然零碎股票交易降低了投资门槛，但它可能会鼓励资本有限的年轻人投资高风险产品。报告称，那些拥有财务安全网的人可能能够在损失后继续投资，而那些没有这种支持的人可能会被迫退出市场。
自 2020 年以来每两年进行一次，今年的调查涵盖了台湾各地 1,070 名 18 岁及以上的人，通过固定电话和手机进行。在 95% 的置信水平下，其误差幅度为正负 3 个百分点。

Public confidence in Taiwan financial services rises to 64.1%: Survey - Focus Taiwan
Public confidence in Taiwan financial services rises to 64.1%: Survey
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
The Taiwan Academy of Banking and Finance. CNA file photo
Taipei, Nov. 2 (CNA) The Taiwan Academy of Banking and Finance (TABF) said Monday that 64.1 percent of respondents to its latest survey expressed confidence in using financial products and services, while university students increasingly viewed investing as a way to save money or hedge against inflation.
TABF held a press conference to release the results of its biennial survey, which this year combined a quantitative survey of public financial behavior with in-depth interviews exploring how university students approach investing.
The survey found that public confidence in financial products and services rose from 38.9 percent in 2024 to 64.1 percent this year. It also showed that 86.5 percent of respondents could comfortably cover their daily household expenses, while 51.6 percent had enough savings to cover at least six months of basic living costs in an emergency.
TABF Chairman Paul Lei (雷仲達) said the improvement in public confidence came amid growing demand for artificial intelligence, record highs on Taiwan's stock market and high real GDP growth.
On financial risks, the survey found that 72 percent of respondents would turn to personal savings, family or friends for financial support in an emergency, down from about 80 percent in previous surveys. Meanwhile, more respondents said they would sell stocks or mutual funds, borrow against insurance policies or take out bank loans, with the rates rising by 3.8, 5.2 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively.
Cheng Han (鄭翰), a member of TABF's management team, said the findings suggested that people are becoming less cautious about the risks of stock investment and increasingly view stocks as a stable source of income.
He advised people to maintain sufficient cash savings to cover three to six months of living expenses, warning that market volatility or a downturn could force investors to sell stocks at low prices and incur losses.
The survey also found that public confidence in avoiding financial scams rose from 65.7 percent in 2024 to 73.8 percent this year. However, people aged 70 and older remained particularly vulnerable, with lower confidence in using financial services and lower rates of electronic payment use age than other age groups.
A bank employee assists a customer in operating an ATM in this CNA file photo for illustrative purposes
Regarding younger people, Cheng said many university students are motivated to invest by concerns that inflation will erode the value of their bank savings, while family, friends and online platforms helped shape their investment habits and confidence.
The survey also cautioned that while fractional-share trading has lowered the barrier to investing, it could encourage young people with limited capital to invest in high-risk products. Those with a financial safety net may be able to continue investing after losses, while those without such support could be forced out of the market, it said.
Conducted every two years since 2020, this year's survey included 1,070 people aged 18 and older across Taiwan, undertaken by phone using landlines and mobile phones. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points at a 95 percent confidence level.
The qualitative research component by Chang Chih-yao (張志堯), head of Shih Hsin University's Department of Social Psychology, involved in-depth interviews with 36 university students aged 19-26 who had actual investment experience.
